items.title: Centrafrique : 12 ans après, les musulmans de retour à Sibut
items.description: Depuis peu, l'appel du muezzin résonne à nouveau à Sibut, en Centrafrique. Le calme est revenu après une guerre civile qui avait poussé de nombreux musulmans à l'exil, permettant leur retour progressif dans la ville. Dans sa petite boutique d'alimentation, Idriss Elder échange avec ses clients, range ses produits et compte sa recette. Des gestes ordinaires qu'il avait arrêté de faire après sa fuite, en 2014. « Comme il n'y avait plus d'entente, mieux valait fuir pour se réfugier ailleurs », raconte le commerçant musulman, de retour d'exil au Tchad. Autrefois symbole du vivre-ensemble en Centrafrique, pays d'Afrique centrale d'environ 5,5 millions d'habitants majoritairement chrétiens, Sibut porte encore les cicatrices des violences qui ont déchiré le pays il y a plus de 10 ans. Située sur un axe majeur reliant Bangui, la capitale, aux villes du nord et de l'est du pays, cette ville-carrefour de près de 40.000 habitants était connue pour ses marchés et pour l'harmonie qui y régnait entre chrétiens et musulmans. « Besoin de paix » – Cet équilibre a volé en éclats avec la guerre civile. La prise du pouvoir par les Séléka, alliance rebelle à dominante musulmane, en 2013, après le renversement de l'ex-président François Bozizé, a poussé la Centrafrique dans le chaos avec une contre-offensive des milices anti-Balaka, majoritairement chrétiennes. Les violences entre groupes armés et les affrontements intercommunautaires ont poussé une grande partie de la population musulmane à l'exil. Dans le quartier Adramane où vivent les musulmans de Sibut, les maisons et commerces ont été détruits ou abandonnés. La mosquée centrale a été pillée et détruite en 2014. 12 ans plus tard, la reprise progressive du territoire par l'armée centrafricaine, appuyée par les paramilitaires russes du groupe Wagner et les Casques bleus de l'ONU, toujours présents dans la ville, a permis un retour de la sécurité dans la ville. Et Adramane renaît doucement. Dans la mosquée centrale récemment reconstruite, les fidèles peuvent à nouveau se retrouver et prier ensemble à l'appel du muezzin. « Ce que nous prêchons ici, c'est le vivre-ensemble, la cohésion sociale et la paix. Nous tous qui sommes revenus avons besoin de paix », explique à l'AFP l'imam de la mosquée, Saïd Goni, vêtu d'un boubou sombre. Lui-même revenu d'exil, il tente de convaincre ceux qui vivent toujours loin de Sibut de rentrer. « Ceux qui ne veulent pas revenir se fient aux rumeurs et ils ont peur. Mais nous les rassurons régulièrement. Nous-mêmes sommes rentrés là où nous vivions avant, il n'y a plus rien de grave », assure-t-il. « Je n'ai plus peur. Il y a la sécurité maintenant et tout est rentré dans l'ordre », abonde Idriss Elder, le commerçant. Mais les traces des destructions restent visibles dans le quartier, qui peine à retrouver son visage et son animation commerçante d'avant la crise. Maisons détruites – « Ce quartier n'était pas comme ça avant. (…) Aujourd'hui, c'est à terre, le marché ne fonctionne même pas normalement, tout est bloqué », se souvient non sans nostalgie Avenir Bissafi, un chrétien qui s'affaire sous une tente en construction. La communauté musulmane, qui comptait de nombreux commerçants, était au cœur du dynamisme économique de la ville. Pour M. Bissafi, la reconstruction d'Adramane passe essentiellement par le retour de ses anciens habitants musulmans. « Nous, chrétiens, avons tout pardonné. Nous exigeons à nos frères musulmans de revenir », dit-il. Selon Ousmane Chaïbou, président du Conseil islamique de Sibut, de nombreux natifs de la ville vivent toujours ailleurs en Centrafrique ou dans les pays voisins. En 2020, l'ONU estime que près de 700.000 Centrafricains étaient déplacés dans le pays et 800.000 réfugiés dans les pays voisins, sur un total d'environ 5 millions d'habitants. La peur n'est pas le seul obstacle au retour. Beaucoup n'ont plus rien à Sibut. « Le vrai problème, ce sont leurs maisons détruites. Jusqu'à aujourd'hui, ils n'ont pas de maison où habiter », souligne Ousmane Chaïbou. Les autorités locales doivent accompagner cette dynamique de retour et consolider la cohésion sociale. Rodrigue Leya, secrétaire général de la région de Kaga, est venu pour cela échanger avec les fidèles à la mosquée centrale et parler de leurs conditions de vie. « Après tout ce qu'on a connu comme crises, certains sont déjà revenus », se réjouit-il. Comme ailleurs en Centrafrique, la stabilisation est fragile. Dans ce pays enclavé parmi les plus pauvres du monde, les richesses du sous-sol attirent les convoitises et les groupes armés qui y opèrent sont nombreux, notamment aux frontières avec le Soudan et la République démocratique du Congo (RDC). AFP

items.title: Osun Election: APM, PDP candidates withdraw, endorse Adeleke
items.description: Two governorship candidates in Saturday’s Osun State election, Adebayo Simon Adewale of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) and Adedamola Adebayo of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), have withdrawn from the race and endorsed the incumbent governor, Senator Ademola Adeleke. Adewale announced his withdrawal at a press conference in Osogbo on Thursday, saying the decision followed extensive consultations with party leaders, supporters and other stakeholders. The APM candidate said his decision was driven by what he described as the need to place the interest of Osun State above personal political ambition. “I, Adebayo Simon Adewale, the governorship candidate of Allied Peoples Movement in Osun governorship election 2026, after deep reflection and extensive consultation with party leaders, supporters and stakeholders, have decided to withdraw from the Osun State governorship election,” he said. According to him, his decision was not influenced by pressure or personal interest but followed his assessment of the political situation in the state. Adewale said he believed Adeleke should be given another term to consolidate the achievements of his administration. “Having carefully assessed the situation, I believe Governor Adeleke Ademola deserves another term to consolidate the progress of his administration as recorded,” he said. He consequently called on his supporters and members of the APM to support Adeleke’s re-election. “Accordingly, I hereby declare my full support for the re-election of His Excellency, Senator Ademola Jackson Nurudeen Adeleke, and I call all my supporters, members of Allied Peoples Movement, and the good people of Osun to join me in supporting the election,” he said. Adewale said his decision was aimed at promoting peace, stability and development in the state. He added: “This decision is about the future of Osun. Politicians should always serve the people, and today I have chosen the path that I believe will best advance peace, stability, development, and the collective interest of our state.” PDP candidate also withdraws In a separate development, the PDP governorship candidate, Adedamola Adebayo, popularly known as Fryo, also announced his withdrawal from the election and endorsed Adeleke. Adebayo made the declaration during a press briefing in Osogbo, urging PDP members and supporters to back the incumbent governor. “I, Honourable Adedamola Adebayo, known as Fryo, hereby endorse His Excellency, Senator Ademola Adeleke, ahead of the August 15, 2026 governorship election,” he said. He called on PDP members, supporters and the party’s structure to support Adeleke. “I encourage all PDP members, supporters and structure to share this position peacefully. Support the emergence of Ademola Adeleke as the governor till 2030,” he said. The withdrawals came less than 48 hours before the governorship election scheduled for Saturday. Adeleke is contesting the election on the platform of the Accord Party, while Bola Oyebamiji is the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and Najeem Salaam is the candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). The post Osun Election: APM, PDP candidates withdraw, endorse Adeleke appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: A nation between adversaries
items.description: PAKISTAN is currently in the global spotlight for mediating between the United States and Iran. Islamabad’s rigorous mediation efforts helped bring about a much-needed ceasefire between the US and Iran in April, which culminated in the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in June 2026. Analysts see the current mediatory position as a new shift in Pakistan’s foreign policy priorities, with Islamabad attempting to assert itself as a middle power and a relevant strategic player in Middle Eastern geopolitics. However, a comprehensive historical analysis reveals that mediation has remained one of Pakistan’s most essential foreign policy imperatives. Pakistan has long adopted an active strategy of mediation to prevent, manage, and settle disputes in the Middle East and within its immediate western neighbourhood. Far from being a passive regional actor, Islamabad has often positioned itself as a mediator in conflicts ranging from great-power rivalries to intra-Muslim problems. This approach is based on a deliberate foreign policy calculus determined by geography, strategic alliances, and the need to protect national interests while expanding diplomatic influence beyond South Asia. The logic behind Pakistan’s mediating role The primary strategic motive behind Pakistan’s mediation diplomacy is the need to keep regional disputes from spilling over onto its own borders. Unlike great powers, which may approach mediation largely for geopolitical or ideological reasons, Pakistan’s security is immediately influenced by conflicts in its near neighbourhood. Regional conflicts have historically been accompanied by refugee flows, cross-border terrorism, interruption of trade routes, arms trafficking, narcotics smuggling, and humanitarian crises, all of which have imposed significant economic and security costs on Pakistan. For Islamabad, mediation, therefore, constitutes a preventive tactic meant to contain problems before they evolve into greater challenges to Pakistan itself. Afghanistan is a glaring example of this security rationale. For over four decades, Afghanistan’s instability has had far-reaching implications for Pakistan, including inflow of millions of refugees, increased terrorism and border insecurity, and enhanced economic burden. As a result, Pakistan expended enormous diplomatic capital in promoting the intra-Afghan peace process, as well as talks between the Taliban and the US. Islamabad’s coordination and facilitation resulted in the 2020 Doha Agreement . These efforts were primarily motivated by Islamabad’s desire to construct a relatively stable Afghanistan capable of denying space to transnational terrorist organisations and minimising fears of long-term instability along the Pakistan-Afghan border. Thus, mediation is a strategic investment in Pakistan’s domestic security. A comprehensive historical analysis reveals that mediation has remained one of Pakistan’s most essential foreign policy imperatives. A similar rationale supports Pakistan’s efforts to defuse tensions in the Middle East, particularly efforts to reduce tensions between Iran and Saudi Arabia. Pakistan shares a lengthy border with Iran while also maintaining strong strategic ties with Saudi Arabia and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states. The signing of the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement in 2025 has further increased Pakistan’s geopolitical stakes in the Middle Eastern security environment, as has the recent mutual defence pact with Turkiye and Saudi Arabia. Any escalation between Tehran and Riyadh could place Pakistan in a perilous strategic position. These confrontations have often exposed Islamabad to opposing geopolitical realities, as well as exacerbating local sectarian tensions. The 1990s era of sectarian violence has had a significant impact on Pakistan’s strategic thinking. Islamabad doesn’t want to allow space for another wave of sectarian violence influenced by the Middle Eastern security environment. This is why Pakistan has continuously pursued a policy of passive or active mediation between Saudi Arabia and Iran. For instance in 2016, when tensions between Saudi Arabia and Iran escalated due to the execution of a famous Saudi Shia cleric, Sheikh Nimr al-Nimr, Pakistan hurried to utilise shuttle diplomacy to defuse tensions. Pakistan’s then-prime minister Nawaz Sharif and chief of army staff Raheel Sharif advocated holding direct discussions between Saudi Arabia and Iran in Islamabad and recommended that both countries establish focal persons to keep communication lines open for dialogue. These activities were widely considered as an effective tool for reducing tensions between Saudi Arabia and Iran. Similarly, in June 2017, a Saudi-led quartet (also including the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, and Egypt) broke diplomatic relations and implemented a rigorous land, air, and sea blockade against Qatar. Saudi Arabia put enormous pressure on Pakistan to take Riyadh’s side. Rather than supporting the blockade, Pakistan maintained its neutral posture and initiated a joint diplomatic push with Kuwait and Turkiye to ease tensions between Qatar and the Saudi-led quad. Although the attempts did not yield significant results, they did reduce pressure on Pakistan’s foreign policy. An Iranian journalist reports from a media facilitation centre during the April 2026 talks held between the US and Iran in Islamabad.—Dawn Library Similarly, following strikes on Saudi oil sites in 2019, the then-prime minister Imran Khan conducted shuttle diplomacy between Tehran and Riyadh in an effort to ease tensions and foster dialogue. Although Pakistan was not the primary architect of the ultimate Saudi-Iranian rapprochement, its diplomatic efforts highlighted Islamabad’s preference for regional de-escalation over bloc politics. More recently, Pakistan’s co-mediation with Qatar in supporting US-Iran negotiations under the Islamabad MoU demonstrated its broader goal of preventing another potentially destabilising conflict in its western neighbourhood. Secondly, Pakistan’s mediation diplomacy strengthens its strategic relevance within an increasingly competitive international system. As global politics grows more polarised, middle powers seek influence through diplomatic rather than coercive means. Pakistan positions itself as a responsible regional partner or net security stabiliser, capable of maintaining communication lines in situations where direct dialogue has become politically challenging. Islamabad believes that successful mediation in regional conflicts can boost Pakistan’s diplomatic profile by presenting it as a proactive rather than reactive actor in regional disputes. This is especially relevant in the context of global preferences to look at Pakistan through the security and counterterrorism lenses. Mediation allows Islamabad to change global perceptions by demonstrating diplomatic ability and a commitment to peaceful conflict settlement. Pakistan also wants to demonstrate its strategic value to major powers through mediation. High-profile facilitation operations, such as organising Henry Kissinger’s secret 1971 visit to Beijing, highlighted Pakistan’s ability to bridge the gap between Washington and Beijing. As of today, Beijing recognises Pakistan’s facilitation efforts, which have improved its status in Washington and Beijing. Islamabad has been consistently seeking strategic goodwill in the international community. States that successfully facilitate negotiations frequently collect diplomatic capital, which can later be used to gain political support, strengthen bilateral relations, or increase influence within multilateral institutions. Pakistan’s active participation in facilitating dialogue in Afghanistan, and encouraging regional de-escalation in the Middle East, allows it to strengthen ties with a wide range of international actors, including the US, China, Gulf states, Central Asian republics, and Muslim-majority countries. The diplomatic goodwill broadens Pakistan’s foreign policy options while reducing the likelihood of strategic isolation. Islamabad believes that an active mediatory role in regional conflicts can protect and further secure Pakistan’s long-term economic interests. Regional instability discourages foreign direct investment, interrupts trade corridors, increases international trade insurance costs, and causes large infrastructure projects to be delayed. As Pakistan strives to transform itself into a regional connectivity hub through projects like the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), peace in neighbouring regions has become an economic necessity rather than a diplomatic aspiration. Stability in Afghanistan is critical for developing overland trade with Central Asia, while lower tensions between the Gulf states and Iran can improve the security of Pakistan’s energy imports, and enhance the utility of Gwadar port. As a result, mediation indirectly helps to create an external environment that promotes economic growth and regional integration for Islamabad. Furthermore, effective diplomatic engagement can boost investors’ confidence by portraying Pakistan as a stabilising rather than destabilising regional actor. International investors often prefer regions with political certainty and amicable interstate relations. Finally, Pakistan’s mediation efforts are motivated by its overall diplomatic identity. Since independence, succeeding governments have continuously prioritised peaceful conflict resolution, negotiation, and negotiated agreements in their official foreign policy rhetoric. Individual mediation initiatives are definitely shaped by geopolitical goals, but Pakistan has often depicted itself as a country eager to provide good offices whenever conflicts endanger regional peace and international security. Whether facilitating dialogue in Afghanistan, encouraging Saudi-Iran engagement, or launching a diplomatic initiative to defuse tensions between the US and Iran, Islamabad has sought to position itself as a bridge between competing actors rather than a participant in regional rivalries. The historical record Pakistan’s diplomatic role as a successful mediator or back-channel facilitator started in late 1969 when Islamabad facilitated the US-China rapprochement. Pakistan facilitated a secret historic visit of Henry Kissinger to Beijing. The visit paved the way for US-China diplomatic and economic engagement, which dramatically reshaped Cold War geopolitics. This episode remains a typical successful example of Pakistan using its contacts to achieve a significant diplomatic outcome. In Afghanistan’s context, Pakistan was a key player in the 1988 Geneva Accords, alongside Afghanistan, the Soviet Union, and the United States. The accords ultimately resulted in the evacuation of Soviet forces from Afghanistan’s territory. This outcome is widely recognised as Pakistan’s most significant multilateral diplomatic achievement. More recent initiatives have produced mixed outcomes. Pakistan facilitated the 2015 Murree peace talks , which were the first publicly acknowledged direct engagement between the Afghan government and the Afghan Taliban. However the process eventually halted. Throughout the protracted Afghan peace process (2009-2020), Pakistan continuously promoted negotiations and backed the Doha Agreement. Islamabad’s initial coordination and efforts to bring the Afghan Taliban and the US to the negotiation table eventually resulted in a US-Taliban pact. However, Pakistan’s efforts did not result in a comprehensive intra-Afghan settlement. Limits of Pakistan’s mediation Despite Pakistan’s long history of promoting dialogue and providing good offices in regional and international conflicts, its overall success rate remains low. According to a qualitative assessment of Pakistan’s mediation record, only about one-third of its initiatives have resulted in concrete diplomatic outcomes, with the majority focusing on confidence-building, maintaining communication channels, or preventing further deterioration of warring parties’ relationships rather than achieving comprehensive conflict resolution. This lower success rate does not reflect lack of diplomatic expertise, but rather the institutional and structural limits Pakistan faces. One of the main issues is that Pakistan frequently mediates highly complex disputes. Conflicts such as the intra-Afghan conflict, external invasions in Afghanistan, Saudi-Iran tensions, Middle Eastern conflicts, and US-Iran tensions involve various stakeholders with competing strategic goals that cannot be resolved only by external mediation. Mediators can facilitate discourse, but they cannot compel opposing parties to compromise when the political costs of concessions are excessively high. As a result, Pakistan’s participation has frequently been restricted to facilitating negotiations, with ultimate decisions determined primarily by warring parties on their own political and strategic calculations. Another important restraint is Pakistan’s low diplomatic leverage in comparison to other regional and extra-regional countries. Successful mediation frequently necessitates the capacity to offer economic incentives, security guarantees, reconstruction assistance, or political assurances that motivate opposing parties to reach difficult concessions. Countries with significantly more financial resources, political power, and diplomatic networks to sustain long-term peace initiatives include the US, China, Norway, Qatar, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. In contrast, Pakistan typically focuses on persuasion, trusted relationships, and geographical familiarity rather than economic incentives. While these assets are valuable, they are largely insufficient to resolve longstanding disputes. Pakistan’s internal security environment further complicates mediation efforts. Persistent tensions with India, ongoing instability along the Pak-Afghan border, menace of terrorism, and periodic economic crises all divert diplomatic focus and reduce the resources available for long-term international mediation. Effective mediation is a long-term process that requires consistent diplomatic engagement, technical expertise, and institutional capacity. Pakistan’s diplomatic machinery usually operates with competing internal and regional environments. This makes it difficult to maintain long-term involvement in various peace processes. Perceptions of neutrality also challenge Pakistan’s mediatory efforts in Middle Eastern conflicts. Theoretically, for mediation efforts to be successful, all parties must believe that the mediator is impartial and trustworthy. However, Pakistan’s deep strategic ties with Saudi Arabia and other Arab Gulf states often cause concern among opposing parties. For example, Pakistan’s longstanding defence and security partnership with Saudi Arabia has historically hampered its ability to be perceived as completely neutral by Iran, despite Islamabad’s consistent efforts to maintain cordial relations with both nations. Similarly, Pakistan’s extensive engagement with the Afghan Taliban has occasionally prompted segments of the former Afghan political elite and some Western policymakers to question Islamabad’s neutrality, even though Pakistan actively encouraged negotiations and political settlements in Afghanistan prior to the fall of Kabul in 2021. These perceptions, whether accurate or not, frequently undermine the warring parties’ willingness to fully embrace Pakistani mediation. The geopolitical climate further limits Pakistan’s effectiveness as a mediator. Many recent conflicts are increasingly impacted by great power competition, and leave little diplomatic space for middle powers to independently secure comprehensive settlements. The Afghan peace process, for example, brought together the strategic interests of the US, China, Russia, Iran, India, Qatar, and numerous other Gulf states. Similarly, the ongoing conflict between Iran and the US is driven by larger issues such as nuclear proliferation, sanctions, Israel’s security, insecurity of GCC states and regional proxy conflict. In such cases, Pakistan can encourage dialogue and propose confidence-building measures, but it lacks the ability to address the underlying strategic calculations that drive the conflict. Another rationale for Pakistan’s relatively low success rate is the nature of the mediation role Islamabad normally adopts. Unlike well-established and well-known mediators such as Qatar, the UAE, and Norway, who aim to reach binding agreements, Pakistan has frequently served as a facilitator, host, bridge-builder, or provider of good offices. These roles are less apparent yet nevertheless diplomatically significant. Facilitators generate opportunities for dialogue, provide conducive environment for dialogue, establish communication channels and decrease misperceptions. Although these measures may not result in landmark peace treaties, they frequently keep preventing crises from escalating into broader armed conflict. Hence, measuring Pakistan’s mediation record exclusively based on the number of signed agreements understates its overall contribution to regional stability. Finally, Pakistan’s mediation activities have occasionally suffered from a lack of follow-up by the opposing parties themselves. Several times negotiations brokered by Pakistan began with hope but later disintegrated due to one or more sides withdrawing due to their domestic political factors or altered external or regional developments. Pakistan’s mediatory experience in intra-Afghan dialogue exemplifies this challenge. Although Pakistan played a crucial role in supporting the Doha talks, the subsequent political trajectory in Afghanistan, combined with deteriorating Pakistan-Afghanistan relations after 2021, proved that successful mediation does not guarantee long-term peace. Similarly, Pakistan’s efforts to de-escalate tensions between Saudi Arabia and Iran in 2016 and 2019 were overshadowed by broader regional forces before China helped broker the 2023 diplomatic reconciliation. Nevertheless, Pakistan’s moderate success rate as a mediator should not be regarded as diplomatic failure. International mediation is inherently risky, and even the most experienced mediators have struggled to reach long-term settlements in prolonged conflicts. Pakistan’s comparative advantage is less in imposing solutions than preserving dialogue when contact between adversaries has broken down. Despite Islamabad’s structural limitations, its geographic proximity, long-standing regional relationships, understanding of local political dynamics of Iran and Afghanistan, and ability to maintain engagement with mutually hostile actors such as Saudi Arabia and Iran are valuable diplomatic assets. As regional crises become more frequent, Pakistan’s role as a facilitator and confidence-builder is likely to remain a significant component of Islamabad’s foreign policy strategy. The writer is a strategic analyst of international security. The views expressed are his own.

items.title: Ouahigouya : Des acteurs des médias en immersion au cœur des chantiers du PMDUVS
items.description: Ouahigouya : Des acteurs des médias en immersion au cœur des chantiers du PMDUVS Ouahigouya, 13 août 2026 (AIB) – Des journalistes et créateurs de contenus de la ville de Ouahigouya ont effectué le mardi 12 août une immersion sur les principaux chantiers du Projet de Mobilité et de Développement Urbain des Villes Secondaires (PMDUVS), a constaté l’AIB. Organisée par le PMDUVS en coordination avec les agences d’exécution AGETIB, ABTP, COPRI et la mission de contrôle, cette visite guidée visait à permettre aux hommes de médias de constater de visu l’évolution des travaux de voirie et d’assainissement réalisés au profit des populations. Le PMDUVS, financé par l’État burkinabè avec l’appui de la Banque mondiale, intervient à Bobo-Dioulasso, Kaya et Ouahigouya. Il vise à améliorer la mobilité urbaine, renforcer les infrastructures de base et accroître la résilience des villes face aux changements climatiques. Sur les différents chantiers visités, le chef de la mission de contrôle des travaux d’assainissement, Valéri Ouédraogo, a présenté les caractéristiques techniques des ouvrages en cours de réalisation. Il a indiqué que les travaux affichent un taux d’exécution de 90% et les premiers résultats sont déjà perceptibles dans plusieurs quartiers autrefois confrontés aux inondations. C’est le cas des secteurs 13 et 4 de la ville de Ouahigouya, où les ouvrages contribuent désormais à une meilleure évacuation des eaux pluviales. Selon le chef de projet à l’AGETIB, Douhari Yé, environ 25 000 mètres linéaires de caniveaux toutes sections confondues, canaux primaires, secondaires et tertiaires, sont en cours de réalisation. « C’est un engagement en faveur d’une communication de proximité, fondée sur la transparence et le dialogue avec les acteurs des médias et les créateurs de contenus. Cette démarche contribue à renforcer l’appropriation des réalisations par les populations», a-t-il expliqué. À l’issue de la visite, des journalistes ont salué l’initiative en estimant d'une part que cette immersion permet aux professionnels des médias de mieux comprendre les réalités du terrain afin d’informer les populations et d'autre part d’impliquer les médias dans le suivi des chantiers en cours. Les responsables du projet ont invité les populations à entretenir ces infrastructures en évitant de les dégrader, de prélever des agrégats dans leurs lits ou d’y jeter des déchets ménagers. Les parents sont également appelés à empêcher les enfants d’utiliser les caniveaux comme lieux de jeux. Agence d’Information du Burkina LG/PN/AS/ATA

items.title: Explained: The Mecca Pact, a safety net with no strings attached
items.description: Rough summary: Enemies will think twice because an attack on one country could drag in all three Takes defense into their own hands as a backup without snubbing the US or leaning towards China. One-on-one rivalries with Iran converted to a three-front headache for Tehran Combines naval power to keep oil shipments and trade routes safe The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, signed on August 7, 2026, by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, represents a watershed moment in the evolving security order of the Middle East. By affirming the collective defense principle that an armed attack against one state will be treated as an attack against all three, the pact has introduced a new bout of debate on the future of the regional order in the Middle East. Early commentary has interpreted the agreement as a departure from the U.S.-led security order and a formal arrival of a “Muslim NATO,” driven by the integration of the Muslim world’s most politically influential and militarily capable states. Rather than signaling a complete geopolitical rupture, however, the agreement represents a pragmatic attempt by regional and regionally adjacent states to hedge against growing strategic uncertainty. From dependence towards regional self-help For now, the U.S. remains central to the regional security order across the Middle East. Its forward military bases, integrated air defense networks, real-time intelligence capabilities, and logistical depth cannot be replaced by any other great power. Even the three signatories to the Mecca Agreement maintain vital security ties with Washington: Saudi Arabia remains dependent on the American defense technology and seeks a civil nuclear deal with the U.S.; Turkey is a NATO member hosting U.S. nuclear weapons on its territory; and Pakistan retains long-standing military cooperation with the U.S., while coordinating closely with the U.S. Central Command across Middle East and Central Asia. The persistence of American military power has not, however, addressed growing regional uncertainty regarding the predictability of U.S. security guarantees. This uncertainty stems from the dual risks of abandonment and entrapment. Regional partners worry that Washington may fail to respond when local territory and critical infrastructure come under asymmetric attack, and they fear being dragged into broader regional conflicts driven by American strategic priorities. Besides, China, the other great power, is neither prepared nor willing to construct an alternate regional order through forward deployments, extended deterrence and maritime patrolling. Even though Beijing has expanded its diplomatic ties and trade across the Middle East, its foreign policy remains focused more on East Asia and the Western Pacific, with a hands-off approach to Middle Eastern regional security. As exclusive reliance on American protection is no longer considered sufficient, the regional and regionally adjacent states are turning toward mechanisms of regional self-help. These new political and defensive arrangements are intended to strengthen their military capacity and complicate the calculations of potential adversaries. The Mecca Agreement enables participating states to strengthen their defensive capacity while operating within the broader context of an American-led regional order. Far from defying Washington, this self-help architecture aligns with the U.S. policy preference for regional burden-sharing, which encourages local partners to assume greater responsibility for their own territorial defense and maritime security. The Saudi security dilemma For Saudi Arabia, the drive toward strategic hedging is driven by the progressive erosion of traditional American security guarantees over the past decade. A series of strategic shocks, including the 2019 Abqaiq-Khurais strikes, the 2021 redeployment of U.S. Patriot missile batteries, and the escalating fallout from the 2026 Iran conflict, demonstrated the limits of exclusive reliance on the U.S. security umbrella. While forward U.S. deployments aim to deter threats, they can also convert host nations into primary targets when Washington enters a broader conflict. While bilateral defense ties and arms procurement from the U.S. continue to be a preference, Ridyah needed to address new vulnerability through geopolitical hedging. The new strategy meant deepening partnerships with Iran’s neighbours: Turkey borders Iran to the northwest, while Pakistan borders Iran to the east. By formalizing a defensive framework with Ankara and Islamabad, Riyadh is seeking to complicate the calculus of Tehran. Iranian military planners considering strikes against Saudi energy assets or urban centers must now account for the political, intelligence, and defense-industrial costs of provoking regional powers situated directly along Iran’s own frontiers. This arrangement achieves deterrence through association, while allowing regional-adjacent states to contribute towards regional stability in the broader Middle East. Besides, pre-pact consultations involving Egypt demonstrate that this emerging regional architecture is not confined to a single agreement or select countries, but it is a flexible arrangement of political and defensive coordination among regional states. Extending maritime security A crucial dimension of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is its focus on maritime security across the Western Indian Ocean, spanning from the Arabian Sea and the Strait of Hormuz to the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and the Red Sea. Historically, Pakistan’s naval posture remained centered on the South Asian theatre, particularly coastal defence along Pakistan’s Arabian sea shoreline. However, the protection of Sea Lines of Communication (SLOCs) passing through critical Middle Eastern chokepoints has become an existential economic imperative for Islamabad, given its near-total reliance on Gulf energy shipments. Under the expanded framework of the MJDA, and building upon the 2025 bilateral Saudi-Pakistan Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement, the Pakistan Navy is deliberately expanding its strategic horizon beyond South Asia. By coordinating maritime domain awareness, joint patrols, and naval exercises with Saudi and Turkish naval forces, Pakistan can actively secure the maritime trade routes that support both South Asian and Gulf economies. Similarly, for Turkey, maritime security in the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa represents a critical strategic vector connecting Eastern Mediterranean commerce to broader Indo-Pacific trade. Ankara’s expanding commercial investments, its naval presence in Somalia, and its export-oriented defense sector make maritime security in the Red Sea a direct national interest. The Mecca Agreement synthesizes the complementary naval capabilities of the three signatories: Pakistani naval manpower and operational experience in the Arabian Sea, Turkish naval technology and warship manufacturing, and Saudi Arabian coastal infrastructure and logistical depth. Together, this trilateral coordination establishes an integrated maritime framework across the region’s vital chokepoints, mitigating threats posed by non-state actors, asymmetric missile strikes, and commerce disruption Concluding thoughts The immediate objective of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is to advance security through complexity, making the strategic environment significantly harder for potential adversaries to interpret. By injecting ambiguity into the agreement, the signatories project collective solidarity while preserving the operational freedom of each government to determine its specific response. This enables Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan to mitigate the risk of abandonment without exposing themselves to entrapment in one another’s peripheral conflicts. An adversary contemplating aggression against one signatory state must now assess whether the action will provoke wider political and military responses, ranging from diplomatic pressure and intelligence sharing to joint maritime operations and direct military deployments. This political association fundamentally alters regional calculations, transforming what was previously treated as a bilateral confrontation into a multi-state risk for Iran, Israel, and regional non-state actors. However, defensive intentions do not guarantee that others will interpret the pact as defensive. Iran may view the pact as an attempt at containment. Israel may view the combination of Saudi resources, Turkish military technology and Pakistani military prowess with growing concern. India will inevitably assess the agreement through the lens of its rivalry with Pakistan. Ultimately, the success of the agreement will depend on whether it can increase the costs of aggression and stabilize the regional order without triggering counter-alignments or an intensified regional arms competition. items.title: Pakistan's leadership stresses need for unity, reforms as nation celebrates Independence Day
items.description: Pakistan’s civilian and military leadership has stressed the need for unity and reforms as the nation celebrates 79 years of independence today. According to state-run Radio Pakistan , the day dawned with a 31-gun salute in Islamabad and a 21-gun salute at the provincial headquarters. A change of guards ceremony was also held at the mausoleum of Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in Karachi. Flag hoisting ceremonies were also held at the Supreme Court and the Federal Constitutional Court in Islamabad. ‘Pakistan’s security linked to peace in our neighbourhood’ In his message, President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to Quaid-i-Azam, those behind the Pakistan Movement and those who sacrificed their homes, security and livelihoods in the struggle for a homeland. “But independence is not only a historic achievement. It is also a responsibility that each generation must carry forward. The Pakistan that was created through the democratic will of its people must continue to grow stronger, more secure and more prosperous. Our task is not only to remember what earlier generations achieved, but to add to it through our own work,” he said. The president said that the past year had reminded citizens of the strength of the Pakistani nation. Recalling last year’s brief military conflict with India, he said, “The events surrounding Marka-i-Haq demonstrated that Pakistan seeks peace, but also possesses the resolve and capacity to defend its sovereignty and national interests. The lesson of strength is ultimately a lesson of responsibility. A country that can defend itself must also use its strength to prevent conflict, protect peace and serve the interests of its people.” He said that the security and stability enjoyed today had come at a great cost, paying tribute to the martyrs of the armed forces, law enforcement agencies and police. “Their courage and commitment have helped safeguard our nation against external aggression and the threat of terrorism. The people of Pakistan remain deeply grateful for their service,” he said. He also highlighted Pakistan’s efforts to facilitate dialogue in the region. “Pakistan has effectively used its channels of communication, its geographical location and diplomatic capital to encourage dialogue and de-escalation at a time when wider conflict could have serious consequences for the region and the world,” he said. He reiterated that all disputes must be ultimately addressed through dialogue and diplomacy. “Our security is linked to the peace and stability of our neighbourhood and the world at large. Pakistan will continue to support efforts that reduce tensions, protect regional stability and create conditions for cooperation,” he said. The president also went on to say that the country must focus on the work that will determine Pakistan’s future. “We must strengthen our economy, create greater opportunities for our young people, improve education and skills, strengthen institutions through a series of governance, economic and social reforms to ensure that the benefits of development and democracy reach every part and community of the country,” he said. “Pakistan’s greatest strength is its young people. Across the country and around the world, they are demonstrating their talent in science, technology, business, education and the creative industries. Our responsibility is to give them the education, skills and opportunities they need to realise their potential. By investing in our youth today, we are investing in Pakistan’s future,” he added. “For ordinary Pakistanis, national progress is measured in practical terms. It means a young person finding the skills and opportunity to build a career. It means a family being able to access quality education and healthcare. It means farmers, workers, traders and businesses being able to plan for the future with greater confidence. The strength of Pakistan will ultimately be judged by whether our national progress improves the lives of its people,” President Zardari said. He also voiced Pakistan’s support for the people of occupied Kashmir, saying Pakistan will continue to support a peaceful resolution of the dispute in accordance with the aspirations of its people and the relevant United Nations resolutions. On Afghanistan, the president said that Pakistan had always respected and supported the national sovereignty of our neighbour Afghanistan and expected the same reciprocity. “It is sad that the current interim regime of Afghanistan is allowing and supporting a cocktail of terror groups to use their soil for launching attacks against neighbouring countries including Pakistan. It is sad the Taliban regime of Afghanistan is collaborating with India in launching terror attacks against Pakistani civilians and security personnel. They are doing this to distract us from the peace building efforts of Pakistan, recognised by the entire world,” he said. “I warn them to stop these evil actions against the people of Pakistan and assure all and sundry that the armed forces of Pakistan are capable of defeating these evil designs,” he said. He ended his message by calling on the nation to contribute to the country’s progress in whatever field they serve. ‘Pakistan committed to defending its national interests’ Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also began his message by paying tribute to the founding leaders of Pakistan, saying the nation owed the fulfilment of its dream of an independent homeland to their vision, statesmanship and sacrifices. Highlighting the government’s economic achievements over the past two-and-a-half years, PM Shehbaz said the country had successfully navigated challenging circumstances to achieve economic stability and was now moving towards becoming a developed economy. He noted that remittances from overseas Pakistanis had increased by $11.3 billion over the past two years, which he termed a reflection of their confidence in government policies. The prime minister said harnessing modern information technology, promoting innovation-driven industrial and agricultural development, creating employment opportunities and establishing a world-class education and skills system remained among the government’s top priorities. Paying tribute to the armed forces, the prime minister said the military, under the leadership of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, had demonstrated exemplary unity and courage during Marka-i-Haq, adding another chapter to the country’s history of defence. He said Pakistan remained committed to defending its national interests, including its right to water resources, and reiterated that the country would continue to play its role as a responsible nation and a stabilising force for regional and global peace. He cited the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye as testimony to the country’s growing strategic role in the region. The prime minister also expressed solidarity with the people of occupied Kashmir and the Palestinian people. He said lasting peace in South Asia was contingent upon a diplomatic resolution of the Kashmir dispute in line with United Nations resolutions, international law and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people. The prime minister also paid tribute to the martyrs of the armed forces and law enforcement agencies who sacrificed their lives for the country, and called upon all segments of society, particularly political parties, to work together for national unity, integrity and the advancement of national interests. He concluded his message by praying for Pakistan’s continued progress and dignity in the comity of nations. ‘Pakistan’s strength lies in the unity of its people’ CDF Munir, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf and Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu also issued a message to mark Independence Day. According to Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the armed forces paid tribute to the Quaid and those whose sacrifices resulted in a sovereign Pakistan. “Their vision, courage and resolve remain a guiding force for the nation and continue to inspire us to uphold the principles and ideals of Pakistan,” the statement said. “The armed forces of Pakistan respectfully acknowledge the supreme sacrifices of our martyrs, the services of our veterans, the dedication of law enforcement personnel and the contributions of every Pakistani who has served the nation. Their courage and selfless service have bolstered Pakistan’s resilience and safeguarded its independence, security and national interests,” it added. “As guardians of Pakistan’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, the armed forces reaffirm their unwavering resolve to defend the motherland against all threats, uphold the Constitution and discharge the sacred trust reposed in them by the people of Pakistan. United with the nation, the armed forces will remain steadfast in preserving peace and stability while creating an environment conducive to national progress and prosperity,” the statement said. “Pakistan’s strength lies in the unity and collective resolve of its people. On this Independence Day, let us renew our commitment to the enduring principles of faith, unity and discipline, strengthen national cohesion, promote tolerance and work together towards a secure, stable and prosperous Pakistan,” it concluded. Dar reaffirms determination to safeguard country’s sovereignty In his message on the occasion, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar recalled Marka-i-Haq and reaffirmed Pakistan’s determination to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity. “We commemorated the first anniversary of Marka-i-Haq, recalling Pakistan’s resolute and successful response to Indian aggression in 2025,” he said in a televised address to the nation. “The occasion reaffirmed our determination to safeguard Pakistan’s sovereignty, security and territorial integrity while remaining firmly committed to international law, responsible state craft and the pursuit of regional peace.” At the outset of his address, the deputy PM extended greetings to Pakistanis and expatriates on the Independence Day, saying we commemorate the day “to pay tribute to Quaid-i-Azam whose visionary leadership, unwavering resolve and steadfast commitment transformed the aspirations for a separate homeland into reality”. He also paid honour to the leaders and workers of the Pakistan movement whose “courage, dedication and countless sacrifices laid the foundations of our independent state”. Dar said that since independence, the country had made “remarkable strides across diverse fields guided by the enduring principles of unity, faith and discipline”. “Today we are a resilient nation of more than 250 million people bound together by our shared history, collective heritage and common aspirations,” he added. He also noted that the country’s achievements in education, science and technology, economic development, sports, culture and other fields “reflect the talent, determination and immense potential of our people”. The deputy PM also mentioned Pakistan’s “strengthened” position on the international stage over the past eight decades. “Our expanding diplomatic engagement, growing economic connectivity and partnerships, and deepening defence and security cooperation reflect Pakistan’s confidence and its commitment to contributing to a peaceful stable and prosperous region and world.” He also mentioned the defence accord signed by Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia last week, saying the “historic agreement reflects our shared resolve to deepen strategic cooperation, strengthen collective security and addresses evolving regional and international peace and security challenges”. He also paid special tribute to armed forces, police and paramilitary forces of the country, saying their “courage, professionalism and unwavering commitment remain a bulwark of our national security”. Dar noted the country always “stood for peace, dialogue, cooperation and mutual respect among nations”. He referred to last year’s conflict with India and said the events “underscored the urgent need of peaceful resolution of longstanding disputes, particularly the Jammu and Kashmir dispute which remains a source of instability in our region”. “Pakistan will continue to extend its principles, moral, political and diplomatic support to the Kashmiri people in their just struggle for the realisation of their right to self-determination in accordance with the relevant UNSC resolutions,” he added. On the occasion, he urged people to “draw renewed inspirations from the ideals and vision that led to the creation of Pakistan”. “Let us reaffirm our collective resolve to strengthen our institutions, uphold our national unity, harness the potential of our people and build a stronger more prosperous and peaceful Pakistan for generations to come,” he concluded.

items.title: Ouahigouya : Des centaines de jeunes en rangs serrés pour soutenir les idéaux de la RPP
items.description: Ouahigouya : Des centaines de jeunes en rangs serrés pour soutenir les idéaux de la RPP Ouahigouya, 13 aout 2026 (AIB)- En marge de la commémoration de la Journée internationale de la jeunesse (JIJ), les participants à l’activité ont organisé dans l’après midi du 12 aout, une marche de soutien à la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP) et leur engagement patriotique en tant que jeunes pour le développement de la patrie, a constaté l’AIB sur place. Cette activité sportive et de maintien a été organisée au terme de la journée commémorative où la jeunesse de Yaadga a fait des recommandations pour son autonomisation socioéconomique et a pris solennellement des engagements. A ce titre la jeunesse de Yaadga s’est engagée entre autres à œuvrer aux cotés des institutions républicaines pour le retour d’une paix durable, d’être en permanence sur le terrain de la sensibilisation contre la désinformation, de soutenir l’action des FDS et VDP, d’être des acteurs majeurs de la construction d’un avenir serein pour le Burkina Faso. Des centaines de jeunes ont pris part à une marche de soutien suivie d’une séance d’aérobic pour marquer leur engagement qui nécessite de leur part de bonnes dispositions physiques et intellectuelles. Cette marche qui a conduit les participants du secrétariat général de la mairie de Ouahigouya à la place de la Nation a connu la participation de plusieurs centaines de jeunes et s’est achevée par une séance d’aérobic à la grande satisfaction des responsables de la jeunesse et des autorités de Yaadga. Agence d’information du Burkina PN/AS/ATA

items.title: IPFLOA founder appeals to P-Square brothers to reconcile
items.description: By Jimoh Babatunde Founder of the Initiative for Peace, Forgiveness and Love for One Another (IPFLOA), Ambassador Kingsley Atoe, has appealed to Nigerian music stars, Peter and Paul Okoye of the defunct P-Square duo, to forgive one another and reconcile their differences. Atoe made the appeal in a message addressed to the two brothers, urging them to put aside their quarrels, disagreements, hurt and bitterness and restore their bond of brotherhood. The appeal comes amid renewed attention to the prolonged disagreement between the Okoye twins. The brothers, who reunited in 2021 after their earlier split, fell out again in 2024 amid disagreements involving their music business and their elder brother, Jude Okoye. According to Atoe, Peter and Paul should remember the years they spent growing up together, working together and building the musical brand that eventually became P-Square. He said their success was the product of the strength, talent and determination of two brothers who shared a common dream. “Peter, reach out to Paul. Paul, reach out to Peter,” Atoe appealed, stressing that their relationship as brothers should take precedence over their differences. He urged the musicians to recognise the influence they have had on millions of young people who watched their journey from humble beginnings to international musical success. Atoe said their reconciliation would send a powerful message to their fans and young people around the world that disagreements do not have to permanently destroy relationships. “Show them that forgiveness is greater than bitterness. Show them that love is stronger than disagreement. Show them that brothers can disagree, forgive, reconcile and come back even stronger,” he said. The IPFLOA founder also urged the brothers to regard forgiveness and reconciliation as a greater legacy than their music, awards and other accomplishments. He said: “Let reconciliation become your new manager. Let forgiveness become your new song. Let peace become your greatest performance.” Atoe’s intervention follows other recent appeals for the Okoye brothers to resolve their differences. Their elder brother, Henry Okoye, recently expressed doubts about the possibility of a reconciliation but nevertheless appealed to Paul to forgive Peter and urged the family to work towards restoring unity. Atoe prayed that God would heal the wounds between the brothers, remove bitterness and restore their relationship. He concluded by urging Peter and Paul to “come back together” and demonstrate that brotherly love, forgiveness and peace can overcome even deep disagreements. The post IPFLOA founder appeals to P-Square brothers to reconcile appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gumi defends public funding of marriages in Shariah states
items.description: Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, has defended the use of public funds to support marriage arrangements in states operating under Shariah law, describing the practice as a legitimate responsibility of government. Gumi made the position known in a statement shared on Facebook on Thursday, arguing that governments in Shariah-governed societies have a duty to address social needs arising from the prohibition of sexual relationships outside marriage. According to him, where prostitution, fornication, adultery and promiscuity are prohibited by both religious principles and state laws, government intervention to assist people who cannot afford marriage should be viewed as part of responsible governance. He said public resources could legitimately be used to support young people in urgent need of marriage, as well as women who face limited opportunities to find suitable spouses. “In a Shariah law-driven state, where prostitution, fornication, adultery, and promiscuity are prohibited by both divine and state laws, using public funds to facilitate the marriage of women who are in excess of the available pool of eligible men, or of any young person in dire need of marriage, is a legitimate and responsible component of good governance,” he said. The post Gumi defends public funding of marriages in Shariah states appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Journée internationale de la jeunesse : Sebba réaffirme son engagement pour la souveraineté
items.description: Burkina-Liptako-Yagha-Sebba-Journée-Jeunesse-Commémoration Journée internationale de la jeunesse : Sebba réaffirme son engagement pour la souveraineté Sebba, 13 août 2026 (AIB) – Les jeunes de la ville de Sebba, dans la province du Yagha, ont célébré, la Journée internationale de la jeunesse réaffirmant leur engagement pour la souveraineté nationale. C’est sous le thème, « Rôle, responsabilité et engagement de la jeunesse burkinabè dans la construction d’un espace confédéral souverain » que cette journée a été placée. La cérémonie d’ouverture a été présidée par le directeur provincial de l’Agriculture, le camarade Mandé Soma, représentant le haut-commissaire de la province du Yagha, le camarade Adama Koussoubé. Jeunes, femmes, anciens, coutumiers, religieux et anciens révolutionnaires ont pris part aux différentes activités inscrites au programme. La célébration a notamment été marquée par une marche pacifique de soutien aux autorités du pays et un match de football. Le haut-commissaire a rendu hommage à la jeunesse du Yagha ainsi qu’à l’ensemble des couches sociales de la province pour leur résilience face aux difficultés. Il a salué leur détermination à préserver l’intégrité et la dignité de leur territoire, malgré les épreuves et les pressions des forces obscurantistes. Le représentant du haut-commissaire a invité les participants à transformer les difficultés vécues en une source de mobilisation pour le développement local, la cohésion sociale et la consolidation de la paix. Il les a également exhortés à débattre des voies et moyens permettant de renforcer la solidarité communautaire et à faire barrage à la lâcheté, à la traîtrise et à l’incompétence, trois maux régulièrement dénoncés par le chef de l’État, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Pour sa part, le représentant des jeunes, Mohamed Diabaté, a appelé la jeunesse à prendre pleinement ses responsabilités dans la construction de l’avenir de Sebba. Il a exhorté ses camarades à travailler, entreprendre, s’entraider et à préserver l’unité de la communauté. « Sebba n’est pas seulement une ville. Sebba est une histoire, une identité, une mémoire et surtout un avenir », a-t-il déclaré, appelant les jeunes à refuser la division, la haine et le découragement. Il a également salué les autorités nationales et locales, ainsi que les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) et les Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP), dont l’engagement contribue à la protection des populations et de leurs biens. Au terme de la célébration, la jeunesse du Yagha a été invitée à se mobiliser davantage pour la paix, l’unité, le travail, la dignité, l’éducation et l’entrepreneuriat, en vue de contribuer au développement de la communauté et à la construction d’un Burkina Faso souverain. Agence d'information du Burkina MMA/AS/ATA

items.title: Le Tunisien Anis Zayana ambassadeur du CIDH en Ouganda
items.description: Le Tunisien Anis Zayana vient d’être nommé ambassadeur du Conseil international des directeurs et hôteliers (CIDH, Malaga, Espagne) en Ouganda. Fort de plus de 30 années d’expérience internationale dans l’hôtellerie, Anis Zayana dirige actuellement le Lake Victoria Granada Hotel à Entebbe. «Je considère cette nomination comme une responsabilité et une opportunité de contribuer au développement du leadership hôtelier, au partage des connaissances, au renforcement des réseaux professionnels et à la promotion du tourisme en Ouganda et en Afrique de l’Est» , a déclaré l’hôtelier tunisien. «Sa vaste expérience professionnelle et son engagement envers le secteur de l’hôtellerie renforcent la vision internationale du CIDH, un réseau mondial réunissant des dirigeants et des professionnels attachés au leadership, au partage des connaissances ainsi qu’au développement du tourisme et de l’hôtellerie» , a noté le CIDH, dans le communiqué de nomination signé parprésidé par son président Vicente Romero Jiménez. II a ajouté : «À une époque où l’innovation, la collaboration et les connexions à l’échelle mondiale revêtent une importance croissante, l’arrivée de professionnels expérimentés issus de pays et de cultures variés continue d’enrichir notre communauté et de consolider notre présence internationale.» Et de conclure : «Merci, Anis, d’avoir choisi le CIDH comme espace de mise en relation, d’échanges professionnels et de nouvelles opportunités.» I. B. L’article Le Tunisien Anis Zayana ambassadeur du CIDH en Ouganda est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Camp Vacances Faso Mêbo 2026 : Dans la Quatrième Région militaire, 464 jeunes campeurs au cœur de la culture du patriotisme, de la discipline et de la résilience
items.description: (Dori, 13 août 2026). La Quatrième Région militaire couvrant les régions administratives de Liptako et de Soum a été choisie pour le lancement officiel national de la deuxième édition du Camp Vacances Faso ce jeudi 13 août, symbole de résilience et de souveraineté. Ce lancement officiel national a eu l'honneur de la présence symbolique d'une forte délégation conduite par le Camarade Ministre d'Etat, Ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense Patriotique, le Général de Division Célestin SIMPORE accompagné du Parrain national, le Camarade Général de Brigade Ismaël DIAOURI, Chef d'Etat-Major Particulier de la Présidence du Faso et du Camarade Directeur Général de l'Agence Faso Mêbo, le Chef de Bataillon Zoodnoma Ahmed SAKANDÉ. La cérémonie s'est déroulée avec la présence des autorités administratives, militaires et paramilitaires de la région. Placée sous le signe du patriotisme et de l’éducation citoyenne, cette édition 2026 réunit 464 campeurs de la Quatrième Région militaire couvrant les régions administratives de Liptako et de Soum sous le slogan «Je m'instruis et je participe à la construction de ma Nation. La Patrie ou la Mort nous Vaincrons !». Elle vise à renforcer chez les jeunes les valeurs de discipline, de civisme et d’attachement à la Patrie. Au cours de la cérémonie, le Directeur général de l’Agence Faso Mêbo le Camarade Chef de Bataillon Zoodnoma Ahmed SAKANDÉ a livré un message axé sur les valeurs citoyennes et patriotiques. « Pendant ce camp, vous apprendrez à connaître et à respecter les symboles de notre Nation, à connaître l’hymne national ainsi que l’hymne de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES). » Le programme de cette deuxième édition prévoit notamment des cours d’éducation civique et militaire, de sécurité routière et d’hygiène. Ces enseignements doivent permettre aux jeunes campeurs d’acquérir des connaissances et des comportements utiles à leur vie en société. Une place importante est également accordée à l’histoire de l’Afrique et des peuples noirs. Pour le Directeur général, cette connaissance de l’histoire doit permettre aux jeunes de mieux connaître leurs origines et de développer leur esprit critique. Pour le Directeur général, l’enjeu est de préparer une jeunesse capable de porter les valeurs de la Nation et de participer pleinement à la construction du Burkina Faso. S’adressant aux campeurs, il a lancé cet appel : « Apprenez. Questionnez. Disciplinez-vous. Connaissez votre histoire. Respectez votre prochain. Aimez votre Patrie. » Le Camarade Ministre d'Etat, Ministre de la Guerre et de la Défense Patriotique, le Général de Division Célestin SIMPORE a,pour sa part, montré l’importance de la jeunesse dans le développement d’une Nation. « Si nous voulons assurer un avenir radieux, meilleur pour notre pays, pour que son drapeau flotte davantage plus haut, un pays moderne où il fait bon vivre, nous ne pouvons nous appuyer que sur les enfants ». Il a par ailleurs lancé un appel : « Nous devons veiller à ce que ces enfants apprennent ce qu’il faut, s’habituent à ce qui doit être fait et s’éloignent de ce qui est proscrit, pour qu’ils puissent être les enfants de demain ». Au-delà des activités de vacances, le Camp Vacances Faso Mêbo entend ainsi contribuer à la formation de citoyens disciplinés, intègres, conscients de leur histoire et engagés pour leur pays. Du 13 au 22 août 2026, dix jours seront consacrés à l’apprentissage, à la discipline et au vivre-ensemble pour les jeunes campeurs, dans l’ambition de contribuer à former une jeunesse consciente et engagée pour la construction du Burkina Faso. DAJC/AFM

items.title: Laâyoune : KBR prend en main le Pre-FEED du projet d’ammoniac d’ORNX
items.description: Le groupe américain KBR a été sélectionné par ORNX Green Hydrogen pour conduire la phase de Pre-Front-End Engineering Design (Pre-FEED) d’un projet d’ammoniac de grande capacité prévu dans la région de Laâyoune. L’étude bénéficie du financement de l’Agence américaine pour le commerce et le développement (USTDA). Conçu comme un projet d’envergure mondiale à faible coût, le site vise une production d’environ 560.000 tonnes d’ammoniac par an et s’appuiera sur quelque 900 MW de capacité d’électrolyse. Son schéma repose sur l’intégration, au sein d’une même plateforme industrielle, de la production d’électricité, de l’hydrogène et de la synthèse d’ammoniac. Le projet doit notamment tirer parti des ressources renouvelables de la région ainsi que de son accès stratégique aux infrastructures portuaires. Une étape déterminante avant la décision d’investissement Le Pre-FEED constitue une phase d’ingénierie située en amont de la conception détaillée du projet. Elle doit permettre de préciser les choix techniques et de faire progresser le développement vers l’étape suivante, le Front-End Engineering Design (FEED), avant d’aboutir à une décision finale d’investissement (Final Investment Decision, FID). Dans ce cadre, KBR fournira à la fois ses services de Pre-FEED et une licence pour sa technologie d’ammoniac. Le groupe américain précise que son intervention doit contribuer à accélérer la maturation du projet, optimiser les performances de l’installation et réduire les risques liés à son exécution. KBR indique avoir déjà déployé ses technologies dans plus de 260 projets de construction, de modernisation ou d’expansion d’unités d’ammoniac à travers le monde. KBR avait également joué un rôle dans l’accompagnement d’ORNX auprès de l’USTDA et dans l’élaboration de la demande de subvention ayant permis d’obtenir le financement de l’étude Pre-FEED. Celle-ci sera menée avec un consortium comprenant GE Vernova, Electric Hydrogen et Terabase, aux côtés de KBR. Un projet tourné vers les marchés internationaux Le développement d’ORNX est conçu pour contribuer aux objectifs du Royaume en matière d’énergies renouvelables et d’hydrogène, tout en établissant une offre d’ammoniac bas carbone à grande échelle destinée aux marchés internationaux. Le projet s’inscrit dans un contexte de demande croissante pour les carburants propres et les matières premières durables, notamment dans les secteurs des engrais, du transport maritime et de l’industrie. Pour ORNX, le financement de l’USTDA et la sélection de KBR constituent un nouveau jalon dans l’avancement du projet à Laâyoune. Peter A. Gish, président-directeur général d’ORNX, a salué le soutien apporté par KBR dans les démarches auprès de l’agence américaine et indiqué que l’étude doit permettre d’accélérer la progression vers le FEED, puis vers la décision finale d’investissement. « Nous sommes très reconnaissants à KBR pour son soutien considérable dans son travail avec l’USTDA afin de parvenir à cette étape importante pour notre projet d’ammoniac à Laâyoune » , a déclaré Peter A. Gish, président-directeur général d’ORNX, soulignant que « ce financement permettra de mener à bien les études de Pre-FEED dirigées par KBR, avec un consortium comprenant GE Vernova, Electric Hydrogen et Terabase. Nous sommes impatients de travailler étroitement avec nos partenaires alors que nous accélérons notre progression vers le FEED et la décision finale d’investissement pour notre projet ». Le projet s’inscrit ainsi dans la stratégie d’ORNX visant à développer une production d’ammoniac bas carbone à vocation exportatrice, en s’appuyant sur les ressources renouvelables de la région. Avec ses 560.000 tonnes annuelles projetées et ses 900 MW d’électrolyse, il constitue une plateforme industrielle intégrée associant production d’électricité, hydrogène et synthèse d’ammoniac. The post Laâyoune : KBR prend en main le Pre-FEED du projet d’ammoniac d’ORNX appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Lutte contre la fraude: 60 millions de F CFA de faux billets saisis par la Douane à Tenkodogo
items.description: Suite aux fouilles d’un chargement En plus de produits prohibés Une procédure judiciaire annoncée Plus aucun domaine ne semble désormais moins ciblé par le phénomène de la fraude au Faso. C’est en tout cas ce que laisse croire une récente et inhabituelle saisie des services des douanes. A Tenkodogo, les gabelous ont, en effet, mis la main sur ce qu’ils n’ont pas l’habitude de saisir en grande quantité : de faux billets de banque. Cette saisie a été présentée à la presse le 13 août 2026, à Ouagadougou. Selon Yves Kafando, l’administration douanière élèvera toujours sa vigilance à la hauteur de l’évolution des modes opératoires des fraudeurs. (Ph. Yvan Sama) L’opération, elle, date de la nuit du 23 au 24 juillet, sur l’axe Tenkodogo Ouagadougou. Selon le directeur général des Douanes, Yves Kafando, tout est parti du contrôle d’un véhicule tombé en panne sur cet axe. Les agents contrôleurs découvrent alors un chargement à bloc de produits prohibés, notamment de la drogue, pour un véhicule initialement destiné au transport des personnes. Une fois le véhicule réparé, il est conduit à la Direction générale des Douanes pour des fouilles approfondies. C’est lors de ces fouilles que les faux billets ont été découverts, dissimulés dans un emballage estampillé contenu « fragile ». Il s’agit de billets en coupures de 5 000 F CFA, révélés faux par les appareils de contrôle des services de douanes. Une procédure judiciaire est ouverte contre M. Tall et tous les mis en cause. (Ph. Yvan Sama) Selon les détails présentés aux journalistes, ces faux billets ne présentent ni de numéros de série authentiques, encore moins de vraies signatures du gouverneur de la Banque centrale. Par ailleurs, cet argent qui n’en est que nom est systématiquement rejeté par un appareil testeur de billets de banque. D’après le Directeur général des Douanes, cet argent risquait d’être injecté dans l’économie nationale et d’alimenter des sources de financement du terrorisme. En dehors des billets, la cargaison, parti d’un pays voisin, comprenait également : 99 plaquettes de Tapentadol d’un poids total de trois kilogrammes et d’une valeur, marché intérieur, de 2.044.350 F CFA ; 360 plaquettes de Vasilium d’un poids total de dix kilogrammes et d’une valeur de 960.000 F CFA ; 10 boules de chanvre indien d’un poids total de cinq 5 kilogrammes d’une valeur de 600.000 F CFA F CFA ; un mini-bus de marque YUTONG , d’une valeur marché intérieur estimée à 10.000.000 F CFA ; 761 colis divers d’une valeur de deux millions 2.000.000 F CFA. La valeur totale de la saisie est estimée à 75.604.350 F CFA. En plus des faux billets, des colis divers portent la valeur de la saisie à plus de 75 millions de F CFA. (Ph. Yvan Sama) A qui étaient destinés ces colis ? Qui en est l’émissaire ? Mystère et boule de gomme, d’autant plus que le chauffeur et le convoyeur ont réussi à se soustraire des enquêtes grâce à leur patron et propriétaire du véhicule qui aurait remercier ses employés dans la foulée. Se prêtant aux questions des journalistes, M. Tall, le propriétaire du véhicule, s’est confondu dans des tentatives de montrer patte blanche. Malien et transporteur depuis plusieurs décennies, c’est ainsi qu’il se présente, le sexagénaire d’apparence a voulu se désengager de toute responsabilité, se contentant des « je n’étais pas là à la saisie », « je reconnais juste être le propriétaire du véhicule », « j’ai libérer mes employés pour ne pas supporter trop de charges ». Pour le DG des Douanes, le fait d’avoir libérer ses employés laisse croire que M. Tall était bien au courant de ce que son véhicule transportait. Selon Yves Kafando, la nature de la saisie ne donne pas la possibilité d’une transaction. « Nous ne pouvons pas transiger sur des drogues, nous ne pouvons pas transiger sur des faux billets de banques », a martelé le patron des douanes burkinabè. Et d’annoncer l’ouverture d’une procédure judiciaire, afin que toutes les personnes qui seront mis en causes par les juridictions puissent être interpellés et répondre des actes qu’ils ont posés. A cet effet, les billets saisis seront considérés comme des scellés qui seront transmis au Procureur du Faso. L’occasion pour le DG des Douanes d’adressé des mots de félicitations aux agents ayant permis la saisie, les félicitant pour leur professionnalisme, leur engagement et leur détermination. Selon Yves Kafando, l’administration douanière reste pleinement engagée à toujours élever toujours son niveau de vigilance face à une évolution des modes opératoires des fraudeurs. Béranger Kabré (Collaborateur) The post Lutte contre la fraude: 60 millions de F CFA de faux billets saisis par la Douane à Tenkodogo appeared first on L'economiste du faso .

items.title: Mobilisation citoyenne pour la réhabilitation du tronçon Villa-Singuidin
items.description: BURKINA-BOULKIEMDE-TRONCON-VILLA-SINGUIDIN-REHABILITATION Mobilisation citoyenne pour la réhabilitation du tronçon Villa-Singuidin Bingo, 13 août 2026 (AIB) – Dans un élan de solidarité et de résilience communautaire, les membres de la coopérative Kogolzanga et la population de Villa, dans la commune de Bingo, se sont mobilisés, jeudi, pour réhabiliter le tronçon reliant Villa à Singuidin. Cet axe, devenu impraticable durant la saison hivernale, faisait l'objet d'une préoccupation pour les habitants. Les leaders religieux de Villa, une centaine de femmes, d'hommes et de jeunes ont pris part à cette œuvre citoyenne exemplaire. Armés de pioches, de pelles, de charrettes et de tricycles, ils ont méthodiquement comblé les creux, les nids-de-poule et autres embûches qui entravent quotidiennement la bonne marche de la circulation. Le Président de la délégation spéciale, Yacouba Gouem, a salué cette initiative. Il a souligné que cette action communautaire, empreinte d'un esprit de résilience, s'inscrit parfaitement dans la vision de la Révolution Progressiste et Populaire actuellement en cours au Burkina Faso, qui encourage l'engagement citoyen pour le développement local. Agence d'information du Burkina AS/PB/AS/ATA

items.title: Abdellah Taïa, écrivain et cinéaste: «Les jeunes Marocains sont oubliés, sont abandonnés, sont méprisés»
items.description: La crainte d'un nouveau drame humain à Ceuta, deux semaines après l'arrivée massive de dizaines de milliers de citoyens marocains dans l'enclave espagnole, de nouveaux appels à tenter la traversée illégale ce 15 août pullulent sur les réseaux sociaux. items.title: Afghan soil being used against Pakistan, Naqvi tells Norway FM as two discuss counterterrorism cooperation
items.description: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Friday met with Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide, where the two sides discussed counterterrorism cooperation, particularly the use of Afghan soil in terror attacks against Pakistan. Eide arrived in Pakistan a day earlier on a two-day visit — the first by a Norwegian foreign minister in a decade. According to a handout issued by the interior ministry, the two leaders discussed strengthening bilateral relations and the regional situation. Naqvi and Eide also agreed to improve cooperation in counterterrorism, prevention of illegal immigration, police training, and mutual legal assistance. The two sides held discussions on the situation in neighbouring Afghanistan and the activities of proscribed organisations operating from the neighbouring country. During the meeting, Eide lauded Pakistan’s “constructive and active” role in the US-Iran war. The two sides also discussed measures taken against illegal immigration to Europe from Pakistan. “Pakistan’s effective measures have led to a 47 per cent reduction in illegal immigration to Europe,” the statement quoted Naqvi as saying, adding that “a zero-tolerance policy has been adopted against illegal immigration”. He said that Pakistan’s measures against illegal immigration were also appreciated by the European Union. “Promoting legal immigration is very important for effectively curbing illegal immigration,” he said. According to the statement, Naqvi told Eide that “Afghan soil is continuously being used for terrorism in Pakistan” and that Pakistan stood “as a wall” between the world and terrorist elements. “Everyone must work together for the complete eradication of terrorism.” Naqvi was quoted as saying. He also told Eide that his visit would be an “important milestone” in strengthening bilateral relations between Norway and Pakistan. In the meeting, Eide appreciated the “active role” of the Pakistani diaspora in Norway and their contributions in sectors ranging from politics to health. Minister of State Talal Chaudhry and other senior officials were present at the meeting as well, the statement added. On Thursday, Eide held a series of engagements with top civilian and military leadership, where the two sides discussed expanding cooperation in trade, investment, technology, climate resilience, maritime affairs, skilled labour and security, while also exchanging views on regional developments.
