items.title: No Adiala visit without confirmation of meeting, says KP CM Afridi
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Mini­ster Sohail Afridi said on Thursday that he would not visit Adiala jail again before Sept 27 unless the government officially confirmed a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan. He also called for the closure of important government offices, including the Prime Minister’s Off­ice, alleging that they had become dysfunctional. Speaking to the media outside Adiala jail, the KP chief minister said the situation at the prison indicated that the authorities had no intention of allowing him to meet Imran Khan. “I have come to Adiala for the last time before Sept 27. I will return only when the government itself confirms the meeting,” he said. It is worth mentioning that Afridi’s name was also included in the list of people who intended to meet Imran Khan on Thursday. Afridi warned that if the meeting was not allowed, PTI workers would block roads across the country from 10pm on Thursday as part of the party’s “D-Chowk” protest. He urged party workers to prepare to take to the streets carrying national and PTI flags, saying the protest would convey a message that the treatment meted out to the country’s most popular leader since April 2022 was unacceptable. According to PTI media cell, protests were held in different cities. Workers went to the chowks and chanted slogans in favour of Imran Khan. Afridi alleged that even government ministers were acknowledging that the country and its system had been paralysed, claiming that the government had failed. He said the people of Pakistan wanted their issues to be resolved and that this could only be ensured by Imran Khan. He said he would march towards Islamabad on Sept 27 along with two million people. Afridi urged PTI workers and the public to focus on Sept 27, describing the date as a “nightmare” for the authorities. He claimed that people were enthusiastic and that a large number of supporters had gathered in Khyber district at short notice on Wednesday. He said a similar street movement would be launched in other districts and claimed that more than two million people would participate in the Sept 27 mobilisation. He added that a street movement would be held in Bannu on Sunday. He said anyone carrying the flags of Pakistan and PTI would be considered a supporter of Imran Khan. The chief minister’s warning came amid continuing PTI protests and demands for access to its incarcerated founder. The Islamabad High Court has ordered the jail administration to arrange meetings with family members and lawyers on Tuesdays and with party leaders on Thursdays, but the orders have not been implemented for several months. Later in the night, while talking to the media, Afridi said there were orders from three judges allowing meetings with Imran Khan twice a week, but the court orders were not being implemented. “We have filed applications in courts for the implementation of the decisions, but the courts are helpless. In that case, we have every right to hold a protest. Even the prime minister said that he would ask about the meeting and then inform me. If such important offices are dysfunctional, they should be closed as they are consuming public funds. Poor people pay taxes and that money is spent on them,” he said. The KP chief minister said even ministers were saying that the system had collapsed. “Today, labourers, industrialists and all other segments of society have been saying that the country is not going in the right direction. Shehbaz Sharif used to say that if he got 30pc support from the establishment, he would deliver and change the fate of the masses, but he has failed despite getting full support,” he added. Published in Dawn, August 14th, 2026

items.title: Transporters’ issues almost resolved: Sindh CM
items.description: • Murad Ali Shah directs transport department to address remaining demands • KATI warns prolonged strike could disrupt production, essential supplies • LCCI calls for meaningful dialogue to end strike; says export containers worth $500 million stranded at factories KARACHI: As the goods transporters’ strike entered its sixth day on Thursday, continuing to disrupt industrial activity and exports, Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah claimed that the dispute was “almost resolved” and only a few points remained under discussion. Speaking as chief guest at the 79th Independence Day flag-hoisting ceremony organised by the Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) on Thursday, the chief minister directed the provincial transport department to make efforts to settle the remaining issues at the earliest so that disruption facing transporters, industries and businesses could end. A delegation of the Transporters of Goods Association, led by Tariq Gujjar, met the chief minister at the KCCI event, where Mr Shah assured them that their problems would be addressed. On the concerns of Nasla Tower affectees, Mr Shah assured the chamber that the Sindh government would examine the matter, acknowledging that they had suffered serious hardship. He said he would discuss the issue with cabinet members to explore possible solutions. Mr Shah also supported the business community’s ambitious vision of increasing Pakistan’s exports from around $30 billion to $100bn, saying the target was “absolutely achievable” if the country harnessed Sindh’s indigenous energy potential and adopted policies to reduce the cost of doing business and make Pakistani products globally competitive, according to a KCCI press release. He said Pakistan had demonstrated its strength on the defence and diplomatic fronts and “the next battle we have to win is on the economic front”. The chief minister called for unity between the government and business community to achieve sustainable economic growth and strengthen Pakistan’s position in global markets. He said Pakistan had the potential to achieve the $100bn export target, noting that overseas Pakistanis were already sending around $40bn in remittances while exports could rise substantially if competitive policies and a conducive business environment were ensured. Mr Shah said Sindh could become Pakistan’s “energy basket”, with vast Thar coal reserves as well as significant potential in solar, wind and indigenous gas. He maintained that inexpensive electricity generated from domestic resources could reduce production costs, improve industrial competitiveness and enable exporters to compete more effectively in international markets. He particularly stressed the need to fully utilise Thar coal to bring down energy costs, saying Pakistan could not afford to neglect a resource capable of providing relatively inexpensive energy. He also called for greater exploration and utilisation of Sindh’s indigenous gas resources instead of excessive reliance on imported gas. Earlier, Businessmen Group Chairman Zubair Motiwala said Pakistan could increase exports from $30bn to $100bn if the cost of doing business and manufacturing was brought on a par with competing countries. He proposed that the government conduct a comprehensive cost-comparison study of Pakistan and competing economies, including India, Bangladesh and Cambodia, to identify factors making Pakistani products less competitive internationally. Industry sounds alarm Separately, Korangi Association of Trade and Industry (KATI) President Muhammad Ikram Rajput urged the government and transporters to immediately resolve their dispute through negotiations, warning that the prolonged strike was severely disrupting the movement of raw materials, finished products, industrial equipment, essential commodities and other commercial goods. He warned that if the strike continued, disruption in supplies of food and other essential commodities could lead to shortages and higher prices. The suspension of transportation could also disrupt factory production, force some industries to reduce output and cause financial losses, he said. Mr Rajput warned that delays in transporting export consignments to ports could prevent exporters from meeting delivery deadlines, resulting in financial losses, undermining the confidence of foreign buyers and affecting future orders. Meanwhile, the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) also urged the federal government to end the strike through meaningful dialogue, warning that the prolonged disruption was threatening the supply chain, exports, industrial production and overall economic activity. Expressing concern as the strike entered its sixth consecutive day, LCCI office-bearers led by President Faheemur Rehman Saigol said the deadlock between the government and transporters could have far-reaching consequences for businesses and consumers if not resolved immediately. Mr Saigol said transportation was the backbone of the national economy, connecting manufacturers with markets, ports and consumers, and any prolonged disruption would create pressure across the economic chain. The LCCI urged the government to adopt a pragmatic and conciliatory approach, address the transporters’ genuine concerns and ensure that industrial activity and the movement of essential goods remained uninterrupted. “The textile industry, one of Pakistan’s major export-oriented sectors, has already reported serious disruption,” Mr Saigol said. According to estimates cited by the chamber, export containers worth around $500m were stranded at factories, leaving exporters exposed to missed shipment deadlines, additional demurrage and detention charges and potential claims from international buyers. “The situation is particularly alarming because the textile sector is currently passing through a crucial shipping period. Pakistan cannot afford to lose export orders or damage its credibility with international buyers because of disruptions in domestic logistics,” he said. Khalid Hasnain in Lahore also contributed to this report Published in Dawn, August 14th, 2026

items.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs0.45, high-speed diesel by Rs1.16
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Thursday raised the price of petrol by Rs0.45 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.16. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs325.43 per litre while HSD will cost Rs383.95 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for August 14 (Friday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Petroleum levy collection hits record Rs1.57tr
items.description: • Cost of running civil govt rises 16pc, crosses Rs1tr for first time • Fiscal deficit shrinks to 2.6pc on the back of provincial surpluses, lower interest bill • Defence spending up 18pc; primary surplus reaches record 2.9pc of GDP ISLAMABAD: With a record Rs1.567 trillion petroleum levy collection amid record consumer-end oil prices following US-Israel attacks on Iran, the cost of running the civil government rose 16 per cent in the fiscal year 2025-26 to cross Rs1tr for the first time despite restructuring and austerity measures, official data showed on Thursday. At the same time, record cash surpluses from the provinces and a sharp fall in interest payments helped contain the fiscal deficit at 2.6pc of GDP — the lowest since FY03 for which comparable data is available on the Ministry of Finance website — while the primary surplus reached a historic 2.9pc of GDP. In its annual report on fiscal operations for FY26, the Ministry of Finance reported that petroleum levy collection surged 29pc to Rs1.567tr from Rs1.22tr a year earlier. It also surpassed the original budget target of Rs1.468tr, which had subsequently been revised upward to Rs1.498tr as part of the FY27 budget exercise. The Rs1.567tr petroleum levy did not include an undisclosed amount of customs duty and Rs26bn collected through the carbon levy. For the current fiscal year, the government is targeting an even higher Rs1.676tr in petroleum levy, besides Rs50bn through the climate levy on petroleum products. Despite restructuring and austerity policies, expenditure on running the civil government increased by 16pc to Rs1.033tr from Rs892bn in FY25, breaching the Rs1tr mark for the first time and exceeding the Rs971bn budget estimate. Defence expenditure also increased by 18pc to Rs2.588tr from Rs2.194tr a year earlier. How­ever, it was only Rs38bn higher than the Rs2.55tr budget allocation despite additional requirements following Indian attacks. Total revenue collection declined marginally to 15.6pc of GDP in FY26 from 15.7pc a year earlier. Federal Board of Revenue collection stood at Rs13.01tr, around 10pc short of target but almost 11pc higher than Rs11.74tr collected in FY25. Despite the revenue shortfall, historically high provincial cash surpluses and a steep decline in interest payments enabled the government to sharply reduce the overall fiscal deficit. The primary surplus — the difference between total revenues and expenditure excluding debt servicing — reached 2.9pc of GDP, the highest since the government began reporting the indicator in FY20. The fiscal deficit had peaked at 8.9pc of GDP in FY19 before falling to 8.1pc and 7.1pc in the following two years. It rose again to 7.9pc in FY22 but has since declined amid successive IMF-backed fiscal tightening. Meanwhile, the primary account remained in deficit until turning into a surplus of 0.9pc of GDP in FY24. It improved to 2.4pc the following year and further to 2.9pc in FY26. Three major contributors to the fiscal improvement were record provincial cash surpluses of Rs1.45tr, petroleum levy collection of Rs1.567tr and a Rs1.939tr decline in interest payments. The finance ministry reported that interest payments fell to Rs6.947tr, or 5.5pc of GDP, from Rs8.887tr, or 7.7pc of GDP, in FY2024-25 — a dec­line equivalent to 2.2pc of GDP in a single year. Subsidies were also contained at Rs1.01tr, almost 22pc below Rs1.3tr in FY25, while development expenditure fell to Rs727bn from Rs786bn. Mainly because of savings on interest payments following the easing of the policy rate from 22pc to 10pc, total expenditure declined to Rs23.09tr from Rs24.16tr in FY25. As a result, total expenditure fell to 18.2pc of GDP from 21.1pc a year earlier. Current expenditure also declined to 16.3pc of GDP (Rs20.69tr) from 18.8pc (Rs21.5tr) in FY25. Defence expenditure, however, edged up to 2pc of GDP from 1.9pc. The four provinces posted a 57pc increase in their combined cash surplus to the Centre, taking it to a record Rs1.45tr from Rs921bn in FY25 — an increase of Rs529bn in a single year. They had committed a surplus of Rs1.38tr under the national fiscal pact. Punjab alone provided Rs915bn — almost equivalent to the combined Rs921bn surplus of all four provinces a year earlier and 163pc higher than its Rs348bn contribution in FY25. Sindh followed with a 24pc increase in its surplus to Rs350bn from Rs283bn. PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provided Rs165bn, around 6pc lower than Rs176bn in FY25, while Balochistan posted a surplus of just Rs20.74bn. On the accounting side, the government reported a record statistical discrepancy of Rs853bn. The discrepancy stood at Rs329bn in FY25 and had drawn concern from the IMF, which had suggested a technical mission that the government declined. The finance ministry attributed Rs448bn of the discrepancy to under-reporting at the federal level and Rs405bn to provinces. It said the federal discrepancy stemmed from “variations on account of time lag in reporting and book adjustments amongst SBP, FBR and EAD data”. At the provincial level, Rs266bn of the discrepancy was attributed to increases in commercial bank deposits, while KP and Balochistan accou­nted for Rs95bn and Rs72bn, respectively, also largely due to movements in bank deposits. Published in Dawn, August 14th, 2026

items.title: Are the Patriot Games Great? No. Are They Fun to Watch?
items.description: How to describe President Trump’s Freedom 250 Patriot Games? The contest, which took place earlier this week, brought students ages 14 to 17 together from across America to answer the question: What if your high-school gym teacher walked headfirst into a pole and was then asked to throw an Olympics with a budget of exactly $6 and three weeks’ notice? Trump boasted when announcing the games that “there will be no men playing in women’s sports,” but after watching almost all of the Patriot Games , I’ve realized he meant that nobody, regardless of gender, would be playing anything recognizable as a sport. When you turn on ESPN’s coverage of the Patriot Games, you see a camera pan slowly over several small American flags stuck into ill-tended grass, while a tune reminiscent of (but legally distinct from) the Olympics theme plays. Welcome to SPIRE Academy, in Geneva, Ohio, where 120 competitors, one boy and one girl from each of the 50 states and … some territories, gathered for the Patriot Games. Are these the best high-school athletes the United States has to offer? In a word, no. Well, is the person representing Massachusetts at least from the state of Massachusetts ? Also no ! Well, does this field of competitors at least look like America? Not the America I remember! But Stephen Miller has been busy. Then what is this? It’s a Trump-produced spectacle, of course! Who chose these contestants? What are they doing at SPIRE Academy, in Geneva, Ohio? And more important, what are these events ? The kids are not the reason that at the end of three days, I feel almost punished for trying to take the Games seriously. I will say that at least the announcers seem to be equally bewildered by what they’re witnessing. Over the course of the games, I notice that their confident proclamations about what is in store for the contestants keep changing from event to event and day to day. Will Victory Hoops (Pop-A-Shot arcade basketball) feature the top-eight or the top-16 contenders? No one seems to know! (It ultimately features the top 16, despite numerous confident announcements and graphics to the contrary.) If you tuned in only to the finale—sorry, the “Freedom Finale”; every aspect of these games has patriotic branding—you might be forgiven for assuming that the Patriot Games leading up to this point had operated on any kind of recognizable human logic. The finale features four contestants competing on an American Ninja Warrior –style course, and the other 116 competitors lined up behind them in patriotic jerseys. They enter the arena to stirring music and dramatic lighting while sparklers blaze. It looks as though things have been running in a professional manner. Someone tuning in just then might imagine that the whole competition featured such standard tests of skill and not events such as Here, Play Dodgeball, and We’ll Give Half of You 30 Points! They have not been watching the Patriot Games like I have. Some elements of the Patriot Games make a minimal amount of sense. The contest, for instance, begins with something called the Presidential Qualifier, with a 100-meter dash, 55-meter hurdles, a Flexed Arm Hang, a Pro Agility Shuttle, a Broad Jump, and a Med Ball Throw. After the Presidential Qualifier comes Dodgeball and Kickball. Each event, as far as I can tell, is worth 60 points. But I could be wrong! The way Dodgeball and Kickball work is that you are divided into six teams (Team Freedom, Team Liberty, Team Valor, Team Honor, Team Unity, and Team Courage, of course!) via snake seeding. Day two offers two of the most spectacular events I have ever seen. Operation Endurance is a military-inspired obstacle course, and everyone is immediately relieved by how much sense it makes. Ropes to climb! An area in which to army-crawl! A jerrican carry! A balance beam! Yes! And you can tell who has won because there is a timer! But then comes … the Varsity Circuit. This is where you can sense things coming off the rails a bit. The event is divided into six stations, each with an activity representing a sport. There are two football stations, where you run through obstacles and then throw a football at a target. There is a volleyball station, where you serve three balls successfully over the net. There is a baseball station, where you whack a ball off a tee and then run the bases. For the soccer station, you kick a ball at a target. And for tennis, the activity is … catching three tennis balls in a row. Catching! That thing you famously do during the sport of tennis! One announcer tries to zhuzh it up a little bit, so we get this amazing description: “They will be stationed about 15 feet away from the tennis-ball launcher. They have to actually receive this, almost like a punt reception, and they have to do that three times.” And while they do this, their families wave signs that say things such as ELIZA IS OUR PATRIOT . Underwhelming as these challenges are, they are also … not that easy for all of the contestants, which means that if you managed to prove your patriotism sufficiently to get selected for the Patriot Games, you’ll most likely win the prize of failing to catch a tennis ball on national television (or at least deep within the bowels of the ESPN app) while the announcer generously remarks that the lights are awfully bright and the volleyball net does seem pretty high. Certainly not a humiliation for you or the president whose idea this was! After the Varsity Circuit and Operation Endurance, we select our top 16, based on total points. Once we reach the top 16, any pretense that this is an open field for competition where anyone can win gets joyfully abandoned. The top-four scorers are all placed on a single team for tug-of-war against the bottom-four scorers, and—you won’t be surprised to hear this!—they win. After this, we have Pop-A-Shot basketball! Yes, the arcade game! “Why can’t they just shoot real basketballs? Isn’t this all being filmed on a basketball court? Isn’t this allegedly an athletic competition?” HUSH! JUST ACCEPT THE PREMISE! THESE ARE PROBABLY THE BEST ATHLETES, AND THESE ARE PROBABLY LOGICAL THINGS FOR THEM TO BE DOING! Look, as someone who has watched Slippery Stairs , a contest in which people try to climb up a slippery stair and some of them fall down and others do not, I understand the power of good announcing to make almost anything seem like a legitimate competition. But the power of good announcing can go only so far, and it cannot do anything when you are watching two students play arcade basketball head-to-head for no discernible reason, and you already know the points will not matter. Trump appears for the Freedom Finale, which has much higher production value than anything that has come before. “I like a lot of finales,” he says. “We’ve got a lot of good finales.” (Did he prepare those remarks?) During the finale, multiple people fall off the Legally–Distinct–From– American Ninja Warrior Race-Course Equipment, allowing their opponents to win. Thrilling! Everyone gets a medal, and the winners get trophies and scholarship checks. Trump stands smiling in the middle of it all. It looks very Soviet, although the Soviets probably would have realized that the tennis-ball catching was too embarrassing to televise. Is this America? No, this is Trump’s America, where everything is made up and the points don’t matter, but our leader still wants you to cheer as if they do. Just don’t tell me these are tests of merit. I watched that Pop-A-Shot basketball! Don’t tell me this is the best we have to offer. And don’t embarrass our high-school students like this. They have enough being thrown at them, between the death lettuce and resurgent measles. The last thing they need is the Patriot Games too.

items.title: Larache : plus de 11.400 tonnes de produits de la pêche débarquées en sept mois
items.description: Les débarquements de la pêche côtière et artisanale au niveau du port de Larache ont atteint 11.407 tonnes (T) à fin juillet 2026, en hausse de 25% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente, selon l'Office national des pêches (ONP). La valeur marchande de ces captures a stagné à plus de 205,01 millions de dirhams (MDH), contre 205,31 MDH à fin juillet 2025, a précisé l'ONP dans son dernier rapport sur les statistiques sur la pêche côtière et artisanale au Maroc. Par espèce, les quantités de poissons pélagiques débarquées dans ce port ont augmenté de 29% à fin juillet dernier à 9.368 T, pour une valeur estimée à plus de 60,85 MDH (+2%), contre environ 59,81 MDH/ 7.249 T en glissement annuel. Les débarquements des poissons blancs ont, quant à eux, progressé de 13% à 532 T, pour une valeur d'environ 26,58 MDH, contre plus de 27,42 MDH en glissement annuel (-3%). Concernant les débarquement des céphalopodes, ils ont stagné à 774 T pour des recettes de 78,83 MDH (-4%), tandis que pour les crustacés, les débarquements ont augmenté de 15% à 733 T, générant des revenus de plus de 38,74 MDH (+8%). Au niveau national, les débarquements des produits commercialisés de la pêche côtière et artisanale se sont établis à 551.547 T à fin juillet dernier, en hausse de 5% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente. En valeur, ces débarquements ont augmenté de 2% à plus de 6,28 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) contre 6,15 MMDH en glissement annuel. The post Larache : plus de 11.400 tonnes de produits de la pêche débarquées en sept mois appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Japan's pacifist course under strain as nuclear restraints challenged
items.description: Standing at a site marked by historical suffering, yet turning a blind eye to the warnings of the future, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has again sparked fresh concerns over her remarks regarding the nation's anti-nuclear principles. At a memorial ceremony held on Sunday at Nagasaki's Peace Park to commemorate the 81st anniversary of the US atomic bombing of the city, Takaichi, when addressing the event, reiterated her ambiguous remarks that Japan "is upholding" the Three Non-Nuclear Principles. Her wording differed subtly from that of previous prime ministers, stopping short of explicitly pledging that the country will uphold the principles. According to the Tokyo Shimbun, since Takaichi took office in October last year, at least 128 local assemblies from 36 prefectures across Japan have submitted written opinions to the Diet, Japan's parliament, urging the government to stand firm on the Three Non-Nuclear Principles. The number marks a record high since the Diet began accepting such submissions in July 2000. The sharp contrast between citizens' calls to preserve the anti-nuclear commitments and voices within the political establishment advocating a review of the principles reflects a profound challenge facing Japan's postwar pacifist identity. Loosening the principles: dangerous test of public acceptance The Three Non-Nuclear Principles, established as a cornerstone of Japan's postwar policy, prohibit the country from possessing, producing or permitting the introduction of nuclear weapons into the territory. However, the principles have now become a subject of open political debate. Japanese media previously reported that officials within the Takaichi administration had considered whether to review the "no introduction of nuclear weapons" clause when revising Japan's key security documents later this year. The issue drew further attention after Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said during a television program in July that Japan should discuss nuclear-related policies "without taboos." Under Takaichi's leadership, the traditional peace-oriented boundaries of Japanese politics have increasingly become tools of political maneuvering, Meng Mingming, an assistant researcher at the Institute of Japanese Studies under the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, told CMG. He said the government's calls to reconsider the Three Non-Nuclear Principles represent a "desensitization test" by right-wing forces – gradually bringing previously untouchable issues into mainstream debate and turning established red lines into negotiable policy options. Remilitarization: Eroding foundations of pacifism The nuclear debate comes amid Japan's broader military expansion. On August 4, the Takaichi government released Defense of Japan 2026, which hyped up a so-called "increasingly severe" regional security environment. The document identified China as "its greatest strategic challenge" while presenting defense investment as beneficial to Japan's economy and society. Takakage Fujita, secretary-general of the Association for Inheriting and Propagating the Murayama Statement, said the white paper was essentially designed to build momentum for revising Japan's three key security documents by the end of this year and advancing further military expansion. Japan's military buildup has become increasingly visible. In March, Japan deployed the Type 25 surface-to-ship guided missile and the Type 25 hypervelocity gliding projectiles in Kumamoto and Shizuoka prefectures, respectively, marking the country's first deployment of long-range missiles with enemy base strike capabilities. According to the white paper, Japan will further expand its counterstrike capabilities by developing air-launched and ship-launched variants of the Type 25 missile, advancing research on hypersonic missiles, and introducing foreign-made stand-off missiles. In April, the Takaichi government revised Japan's three principles on transfer of defense equipment and technology, allowing exports of lethal weapons in principle. Fujita described the move as a reversal of Japan's postwar pacifist course and "a reckless move that opens the door to war." Japan's defense budget for fiscal 2027 is expected to reach around 8.9 trillion yen (around $55.9 billion), with a senior government official suggesting the final amount could rise to 10 trillion yen (around $62.8 billion), setting another record. Makoto Ito, director of the Japan Institute of Constitutional Law, warned that the white paper's emphasis on boosting "comprehensive national power" to address so-called security challenges could bring civilian technologies and social resources into the defense framework, reflecting a dangerous drive toward remilitarization. Public and regional concerns Meanwhile, anti-war sentiment remains strong among sections of Japanese society. At the Nagasaki memorial ceremony, Mayor Shiro Suzuki called nuclear weapons an "absolute evil" and urged the Japanese government to fulfill its historical responsibility. On May 3, Constitution Memorial Day, around 50,000 people gathered in Tokyo to defend Japan's pacifist Constitution. The BBC reported that Japan has witnessed some of the largest anti-war demonstrations in decades, with protests spreading from Tokyo to Osaka, Kyoto and Fukuoka. Meng said the contrast between public sentiment and the government's security agenda reveals a deep divide between Japanese society and right-wing political forces represented by Takaichi. He said Japan's current push for military expansion is being driven largely by conservative forces seeking to reshape the country's long-standing peace consensus. Also, as the only country to have suffered nuclear attacks, Japan's nuclear policy choices carry implications beyond domestic politics and are closely tied to regional stability in Northeast Asia and the foundation of the international nuclear non-proliferation regime. Japan had refused to reflect on its wartime history while repeatedly fabricating narratives about threats from neighboring countries to justify military expansion. He warned that Japan's remilitarization had become a real threat to regional peace and stability, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said. Russian Ambassador to Japan Nikolai Nozdrev said abandoning the Three Non-Nuclear Principles would directly violate Japan's international obligations as a non-nuclear state under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons and could seriously worsen security tensions in the Asia-Pacific region, prompting countermeasures from other countries.

items.title: Punjab govt launches ‘paperless governance’
items.description: LAHORE: Punjab goes paperless as Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Thursday launched “government-to-government, government-to-business and government-to-citizen” services. The CM said the Punjab government had become the first province to establish e-FOAS, e-Procurement, e-Pay, e-Auction, OneMap, HRMIS and a data warehouse. She presided over an online meeting to review the progress in digitalisation and the automation. Chairman Punjab Information Technology Board (PITB) Faisal Yousaf briefed the participants. The CM directed the PITB to take steps for importing paperless automation software and ordered continuous feedback from applicants. She said that an end-to-end automated paperless system would prove effective in eliminating corruption. “We want to save people from the inconvenience of visiting government offices for even minor tasks.” Ms Nawaz said services provided through a digital automation system without requiring applicants to reveal their identity would help eliminate corrupt elements. “We are putting every sector, every department and every institution of Punjab on the path to digitalisation,” she declared and added that the entire team was working as one unit for digitalisation and automation. She said automation services system eliminated the need for interaction with government officials, thereby ensuring transparency. The meeting was informed that more than 6,000 systems had been connected with the PITB’s central system in the province, while 600 organisations and institutions had been digitally connected through e-FOAS. The e-filing system had issued 176,173 summary notices and resulted in savings of Rs9.1m. The briefing further revealed that smart monitoring of development projects had established a new benchmark for transparency in development schemes. More than 25,000 suppliers had been connected with the province-wide e-procurement system, under which digital purchases worth Rs6tr and 1.29m tenders had been processed. “The e-Procurement system had introduced a transparent, end-to-end tendering mechanism without requiring applicants to visit any government office, resulting in savings of Rs1.3 million. Revenue collection through transactions had reached Rs1.137bn,” the meeting was told. Published in Dawn, August 14th, 2026

items.title: SC judges’ pay, benefits raised to FCC-level
items.description: • Judges’ salaries raised to Rs1.5m per month • Afridi to remain ‘CJP’ until retirement, title will subsequently go to whoever is senior among FCC and SC chief justices ISLAMABAD: President Asif Ali Zar­dari has approved an increase in the salaries, judicial allowance and pension benefits of Supreme Court judges, bringing them at par with those of judges of the newly constituted Federal Constitu­tional Court (FCC), effective from Dec 10, 2025. Under the Salary of Judges of the Supreme Court Order, 2026, the monthly salary of Supreme Court judges has been increased to Rs1.5 million from the earlier Rs1.16m. The order will come into force immediately and will be deemed to have taken effect from Dec 10, 2025. However, Chief Justice Yahya Afridi will receive a monthly salary of Rs1.6m, although the order specifies Rs1.55 million as the salary of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court. Justice Yahya Afridi will receive the enhanced salary of Rs1.6m as he has been designated as the Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP). He will also retain the coveted title of CJP until his superannuation on Oct 26, 2027, following a last-minute change introduced through the 27th Constitution Amendment. Earlier, it was believed that the title would eventually go to the chief justice of the FCC. The substitution made in Clause 23 of Article 176 clarifies that the incumbent Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, who is Justice Yahya Afridi, will continue to hold the title of CJP for the remainder of his term. Justice Afridi was sworn in as the 30th Chief Justice of Pakistan in October 2024, for a three-year term. Another provision introduced through the amendment defines the CJP, after the retirement of the incumbent, as the senior of the two chief justices — that is, the chief justices of the FCC and the Supreme Court. This provision will come into effect after the retirement of the incumbent CJP. The issue was further clarified when Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar rejected the impression that the 27th Amendment had abolished the office of the CJP. Speaking on the floor of the National Assembly, the law minister said the office had not been abolished and that CJP Afridi would continue to head key judicial bodies, including the Supreme Judicial Council (SJC) and the Judicial Commission of Pakistan. After his retirement, however, the position of CJP will go to whichever of the two chief justices — of the FCC or the Supreme Court — is senior. To increase the salary of the CJP, the president also approved the Chief Justice of Pakistan Order, 2026, which will be deemed to have taken effect from July 1, 2026. Likewise, under the Supreme Court Judges (Leave, Pension and Privileges) (Amendment) Order, 2026, which will also take effect from Dec 10, 2025, an amendment has been made to paragraph 22, under which a judge will be entitled to a monthly superior judicial allowance of Rs1.5m. Similarly, an amendment to paragraph 16 provides that the pension of the Chief Justice and judges of the Supreme Court will be calculated at 85pc and 75pc, respectively, of the salary as determined by the president. In addition, paragraph 19 has been amended by inserting a provision under which a judge will be entitled to a monthly medical allowance of Rs150,000. Published in Dawn, August 14th, 2026

items.title: Brahim Diaz : « Je suis heureux avec Mourinho et le Real Madrid »
items.description: Brahim Diaz affiche sa satisfaction à l’approche de la nouvelle saison. L’international marocain estime retrouver progressivement ses meilleures sensations et se dit heureux au Real Madrid, sous la direction de José Mourinho et aux côtés de ses coéquipiers. Arrivé depuis une semaine avec ses coéquipiers pour préparer la nouvelle saison, Brahim Díaz estime que les séances d’entraînement lui permettent de monter progressivement en puissance. « Je me sens bien. Nous sommes arrivés il y a une semaine et je sens que je progresse progressivement avec le travail. Je suis heureux avec l’entraîneur, le staff et les joueurs » , a déclaré le Marocain après la rencontre. Le joueur de 27 ans entend profiter pleinement de cette période de préparation pour retrouver son meilleur niveau. L’enchaînement des entraînements et des matches doit lui permettre de gagner progressivement en rythme et en confiance. Brahim Diaz se montre également satisfait de l’ambiance au sein du vestiaire madrilène, alors que le Real Madrid prépare une saison particulièrement ambitieuse. Face au Deportivo La Corogne, le Lion de l'Atlas s’est également illustré en inscrivant un joli but. « Lunin m’a vu dans une bonne position et m’a donné le ballon. Je pense que le contrôle de la poitrine m’a donné un avantage pour continuer ma course. Ensuite, je l’ai poussé devant moi et j’ai bien terminé l’action. C’est un beau but, mais le mérite revient aussi à Lunin », a expliqué l’international marocain. Cette réalisation vient récompenser son travail durant la préparation et constitue un signal positif avant le début de la saison. Le Real Madrid veut continuer à écrire l’histoire Brahim Díaz affiche également de grandes ambitions pour les mois à venir. Conscient des exigences qui accompagnent le maillot du Real Madrid, le Marocain veut contribuer aux succès du club. « Ce sera une belle année, une année exceptionnelle. C’est le Real Madrid et nous voulons continuer à écrire l’histoire » , a-t-il lancé. Une déclaration qui témoigne de l’état d’esprit du joueur et des ambitions du vestiaire madrilène. Diaz entend désormais poursuivre sa progression au fil des prochaines semaines afin d’atteindre sa pleine forme et de jouer un rôle important dans les objectifs du Real Madrid cette saison. Après une préparation encourageante et un but face au Deportivo, le Marocain veut désormais transformer cette bonne dynamique en performances régulières sous les couleurs madrilènes. The post Brahim Diaz : « Je suis heureux avec Mourinho et le Real Madrid » appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Flash
items.description: Longtemps considérée comme un sujet secondaire, la santé mentale occupe aujourd’hui une place importante dans les préoccupations sociales. Stress, anxiété, solitude, fatigue émotionnelle ou encore dépression touchent de nombreuses personnes, notamment les jeunes, souvent confrontés aux pressions liées aux études, au travail, aux relations sociales et aux incertitudes de l’avenir. Pourtant, beaucoup choisissent de garder leurs souffrances en silence, par peur du jugement ou par manque d’écoute. Ce constat révèle une réalité préoccupante : derrière certains sourires, peuvent se cacher des combats intérieurs difficiles à supporter. La santé mentale mérite autant d’attention que la santé physique. Parler de ses difficultés, chercher du soutien auprès de proches ou de professionnels et prendre du temps pour soi ne sont pas des signes de faiblesse, mais des actes de responsabilité envers soi-même. Prendre soin de son mental, c’est aussi préserver sa vie. Chacun doit apprendre à écouter ses émotions, à respecter ses limites et à comprendre qu’il n’est pas nécessaire d’affronter seul les épreuves. Une personne en paix avec elle-même est mieux préparée à construire son avenir et à contribuer positivement à sa communauté. Ange BONTOGO (Stagiaire)

items.title: Souveraineté énergétique et minière : faire des ressources naturelles, la force motrice d’un Sahel nouveau
items.description: La première rencontre des ministres chargés de l’Energie, des Mines et du Pétrole des pays de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel s’est tenue sous le patronage du Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, jeudi 13 août 2026 à Ouagadougou. La révolution que portent les pays de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel (AES) ne saurait être complète sans une révolution dans la gouvernance des ressources naturelles. C’est conscient de cela que les ministres chargés de l’Energie, des Mines et du Pétrole des pays membres ont tenu leur première rencontre, jeudi 13 août 2026 à Ouagadougou. Présidée par le Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, elle a regroupé des délégations du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger. Selon le chef du gouvernement, hauts fonctionnaires et experts des trois pays ont travaillé du 10 août au 13 août 2026 sur des documents structurants pour donner un contenu réel, concret et opérationnel à la souveraineté sur les ressources énergétiques, minières et pétrolières de l'espace AES. Il s'agit notamment du cadre général d’exploitation des ressources énergétiques et minières, des cadres harmonisés des politiques énergétiques et minières, ainsi qu’un mémorandum d’entente relatif à l’institution de la Semaine de l’énergie et des mines de l’AES. Pour le ministre nigérien des Mines, le commissaire-colonel Abarchi Ousmane, le véritable défi est de transformer davantage. Il a précisé que ces textes ne doivent pas être perçus comme de simples documents administratifs ou comme des actes protocolaires. « Ils doivent être des instruments d’action économique, des outils de souveraineté et des repères pour l’édification d’un Sahel nouveau », a-t-il déclaré. Pour lui, l’ambition est de bâtir un Sahel où l’électricité éclaire les villes comme les villages, l’énergie alimente les unités de production, les écoles, les centres de santé et les infrastructures de sécurité et les ressources minières transformés au bénéfice des peuples. Transformer davantage Le Premier ministre a indiqué que dans le domaine pétrolier, l’aspiration est de sécuriser les corridors d’approvisionnement ; mutualiser les capacités de stockage, de transport, de raffinage ; renforcer la transparence de la chaîne de distribution et réduire durablement l’exposition aux chocs extérieurs. Pour atteindre cet objectif, il a appelé les Etats à combattre les pratiques de prédation, les trafics illicites, la fraude, l’évasion des revenus et toutes les formes de spoliation des patrimoines nationaux. Le ministre des Mines du Niger, le commissaire-colonel Abarchi Ousmane, a fait savoir que le véritable défi n'est pas d’extraire davantage mais de transformer plus. Pour le ministre nigérien des Mines, le commissaire-colonel Abarchi Ousmane, le véritable défi est de transformer davantage. De sa conviction, les ressources doivent être pensées comme un patrimoine commun de développement et l’énergie doit être la véritable monnaie du développement. Le ministre des Mines du Mali, Amadou Keïta, a souligné la nécessité de doter l’AES de projets structurants et intégrateurs dans les secteurs stratégiques comme l’énergie, le pétrole et les mines permettant de soutenir sa souveraineté économique. Le Mali s’inscrit dans la dynamique de cadrage en vue de bâtir un socle solide à la coopération au sein de l’AES dans le secteur des mines et de l’énergie, a affirmé le ministre malien. Il a notifié que la transformation économique doit s’accompagner d’une gouvernance plus rigoureuse. Aly SAWADOGO Martin OUEDRAOGO (Stagiaire)

items.title: Première commission mixte de coopération Burkina-Burundi : 14 accords signés
items.description: C'est avec une grande satisfaction que s'est achevée la toute première session de la commission mixte de coopération entre le Burkina Faso et la République du Burundi, le 13 août 2026 dans la capitale burundaise. Les travaux intenses et interactifs des experts se sont soldés par 14 accords de coopération, signés par les ministres des Affaires étrangères burkinabè et burundais lors de la cérémonie de clôture. Il s'agit de l’accord de coopération entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi en matière d’agriculture et d’élevage, d’accord de coopération entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi en matière de sécurité, l’accord de coopération entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi dans le domaine de la protection civile, l’accord de coopération relatif aux services aériens entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi, l’accord de coopération en matière de santé entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi, l’accord de coopération en matière d’emploi entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi, l’accord de coopération en matière de travail et de protection sociale entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi, l’accord de coopération en matière de jeunesse entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi, l’accord de coopération dans le domaine du sport et des suppression de visa en faveur des ressortissants des deux pays titulaires de passeport diplomatique, de passeport de service ou de passeport ordinaire, l’accord de coopération entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi en matière de prévention des risques et gestion des catastrophes, l’accord de coopération entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi en matière d’enseignement et de formation techniques et professionnels, l’accord de coopération entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi dans les domaines de l'enseignement supérieur et de la recherche et l’accord de coopération entre le gouvernement du Burkina Faso et le gouvernement de la République du Burundi sur la reconnaissance réciproque et l’échange de permis de conduire nationaux. Insuffler une dynamique nouvelle Ces nouveaux instruments juridiques contribueront à insuffler une dynamique nouvelle à une coopération scellée depuis près de trois décennies, pour davantage d'actions de développement au profit des peuples burundais et burkinabè. Dans une convergence de vues, les deux chefs de délégations se sont réjouis de cette nouvelle étape qui vient d'être amorcée et ont émis le vœu qu' elle se consolide dans la durée. Pour le chef de la diplomatie burkinabè, après cette étape, c'est maintenant que le vrai travail commence à travers des actions concrètes sur le terrain. « La signature de ce jour n'est pas un aboutissement : c'est un point de départ. Nous devons poursuivre, sans relâche, les concertations, en vue d'une bonne mise en œuvre des instruments juridiques qui viennent d'être signés. Une Commission mixte n'est pas une simple formalité diplomatique : c'est un outil de gouvernance de la coopération, l'instance où l'intention politique de nos chefs d'Etat se transforme en programmes concrets, en projets mesurables, en résultats tangibles pour nos populations », soutient le camarade ministre des Affaires étrangères burkinabè, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré. Reconnaissant également la nécessité d'aller vite et bien dans la concrétisation des accords signés, le ministre des Affaires de la République du Burundi encourage son pays et le Burkina Faso à dorénavant compter l’un sur l’autre et explorer les possibilités d’une coopération Sud-Sud fondée sur la confiance, le respect mutuel, la solidarité et la recherche d’intérêts communs. « Nous devons engager des échanges entre opérateurs économiques, promouvoir les investissements réciproques, développer les partenariats entre les secteurs privés, faciliter la circulation des biens et des services et mieux faire connaître les opportunités qu’offrent nos deux économies. Nous devons également accorder une place de choix à la jeunesse qui constitue à la fois la principale force vive de nos nations et le moteur de leur avenir », a indiqué le ministre Edouard Bizimana. Rappelons que c'est en droite ligne des très hautes instructions données par les Présidents Ibrahim Traoré du Burkina Faso et Evariste Ndayishimiyé du Burundi que s'est tenue la présente session de la commission de Coopération entre les deux pays. Elle traduit ainsi une ambition claire et partagée de faire de la coopération entre le Burundi et le Burkina Faso une référence de la coopération Sud-Sud, bâtie sur les fondamentaux que sont l'intégration régionale et la paix. Pour une mise en œuvre effective des accords signés, les deux parties ont décidé de la formalisation diligente des comités sectoriels de suivi des engagements. DCRP/MAE

items.title: AES: « Nos ressources ne doivent plus être considérées comme de simples marchandises destinées à alimenter les industries et la prospérité des autres »
items.description: Réunis à Ouagadougou, les ministres de l’Énergie, des Mines et du Pétrole du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger posent les bases d’une exploitation concertée des ressources pour renforcer la souveraineté économique du Sahel. La Confédération des États du Sahel (AES) a franchi une nouvelle étape dans sa quête de souveraineté économique. Jeudi 13 août, Ouagadougou a accueilli la première rencontre des ministres en charge de l’Énergie, des Mines, des Carrières et du Pétrole du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger. Sous le haut patronage du Premier ministre Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, les trois délégations ont affirmé leur volonté de transformer leurs ressources naturelles en moteurs d’industrialisation et de développement. Dans son discours d’ouverture, le Chef du Gouvernement a insisté sur l’importance stratégique de cette coopération : « Nos ressources doivent devenir le levier de notre souveraineté, le moteur de notre transformation économique et le socle de notre justice sociale. » Depuis le 10 août, les experts des trois pays ont travaillé à l’élaboration de cadres harmonisés pour les politiques énergétique et minière, ainsi qu’à un mémorandum instituant la future Semaine de l’Énergie et des Mines de l’AES. Ces instruments visent à améliorer l’accès à une énergie fiable, accélérer l’interconnexion des réseaux, mutualiser les capacités de production et promouvoir les énergies renouvelables. Dans le secteur pétrolier, les États entendent sécuriser les corridors d’approvisionnement, renforcer les capacités de stockage et développer à terme des unités de raffinage. Côté mines, la priorité est donnée à la transformation locale des matières premières, à la traçabilité des flux et à une meilleure mobilisation des revenus. Le ministre nigérien des Mines, Ousmane Abarchi, a résumé l’enjeu : « Notre véritable défi n’est plus d’extraire davantage, il est de transformer davantage. » Il a défendu l’idée d’une « civilisation énergétique du Sahel », fondée sur la mise en commun des potentialités régionales : solaire, éolien, gaz, pétrole, uranium et charbon. Son homologue malien, le Pr Amadou Keïta, a pour sa part appelé à doter la Confédération de projets structurants et intégrateurs capables de soutenir durablement la souveraineté économique. Au-delà des ambitions, le Premier ministre burkinabè a insisté sur la nécessité d’une gouvernance rigoureuse : transparence des contrats, maîtrise des données géologiques, lutte contre la fraude et protection de l’environnement. L’objectif est clair : que l’or, le lithium, l’uranium, le fer, le phosphate et le pétrole contribuent directement à la création d’emplois, au financement des infrastructures et à l’amélioration des conditions de vie. « Nos populations ne nous jugeront pas sur la beauté de nos textes, mais sur les résultats concrets obtenus », a rappelé le Chef du Gouvernement. Ces résultats devront se traduire par une énergie plus disponible, des coûts maîtrisés, une sécurisation des approvisionnements et une transformation accrue des matières premières. En choisissant de valoriser ensemble leurs ressources, le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger affirment leur volonté de bâtir une souveraineté économique tangible. Pour l’AES, l’enjeu est désormais de transformer cette ambition en bénéfices concrets pour les populations du Sahel. L’article AES: « Nos ressources ne doivent plus être considérées comme de simples marchandises destinées à alimenter les industries et la prospérité des autres » est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Protection de l’économie nationale : La Douane burkinabè intensifie la traque des réseaux de fraude, 60 millions de faux billets stoppés
items.description: La fraude économique, commerciale et financière change de visage, mais la riposte de la Douane burkinabè ne faiblit pas. À mesure que les réseaux criminels diversifient leurs modes opératoires, les services douaniers renforcent leur vigilance et affinent leurs techniques de contrôle. La saisie, le 23 juillet 2026 à Tenkodogo, de 60 millions de francs CFA en faux billets, dissimulés dans un bus de transport en commun, en fournit une nouvelle illustration spectaculaire. Présentés ce jeudi 13 août 2026 par la Direction générale des Douanes (DGD), les résultats de cette opération donnent la mesure des enjeux auxquels sont confrontés les agents chargés de protéger l’économie nationale. Au-delà des faux billets, plusieurs produits prohibés ont été découverts à bord du véhicule, portant la valeur marchande intérieure de l’ensemble des marchandises et du moyen de transport saisis à 75 604 350 francs CFA. Une cargaison qui en cache une autre. L’affaire commence par le contrôle d’un bus immatriculé BE 4881 RB, de marque Yutong. Le véhicule, intercepté à Tenkodogo, devait être acheminé à Ouagadougou pour des vérifications complémentaires. Mais le trajet vers la capitale prend une tournure inattendue. Le bus tombe en panne à Toécé, à environ 80 kilomètres de Ouagadougou. Le 25 juillet, il est placé sous la garde de la gendarmerie et des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP) de la localité, le temps de sa réparation. Il ne rejoindra finalement la Direction générale des Douanes que le 31 juillet. C’est alors qu’une fouille approfondie des colis fait tomber le masque. Dans un carton présenté comme contenant un « objet fragile », les agents découvrent des billets de banque en coupures de 5 000 francs CFA. Les appareils de contrôle douanier ne tardent pas à livrer leur verdict : les billets sont faux. Au total, 12 kilogrammes de faux billets, représentant une valeur nominale de 60 millions de francs CFA, sont saisis. Une découverte particulièrement préoccupante au regard du risque que représente l’introduction de fausse monnaie dans le circuit économique. En stoppant cette cargaison, les services douaniers ont ainsi contribué à empêcher que des sommes frauduleuses ne viennent contaminer les transactions économiques et fragiliser davantage la confiance dans les moyens de paiement. Une saisie qui dévoile l’ingéniosité des réseaux de fraude Faux billets, stupéfiants et produits prohibés… La fouille ne s'arrête pas aux billets contrefaits. Les agents mettent également la main sur 99 plaquettes de Tapentadol, d’un poids de trois kilogrammes, dont la valeur marchande intérieure est estimée à 2 044 350 francs CFA. S’y ajoutent 360 plaquettes de Vasilium, représentant dix kilogrammes et évaluées à 960 000 francs CFA, ainsi que dix boules de chanvre indien, d’un poids total de cinq kilogrammes, pour une valeur estimée à 600 000 francs CFA. Le véhicule lui-même, évalué à 10 millions de francs CFA, entre dans le décompte des saisies, de même qu’une déclaration IM8 du 22 juillet 2025 portant sur 761 colis divers, estimés à deux millions de francs CFA. L’opération révèle donc un phénomène qui dépasse largement la simple contrebande de marchandises : les circuits clandestins semblent désormais susceptibles de transporter, dans un même flux, des produits commerciaux, des substances prohibées et de la fausse monnaie. Depuis un certain temps, la Douane burkinabè fait face à des fraudeurs de plus en plus ingénieux. Pour la Direction générale des Douanes, cette affaire illustre surtout la nécessité d’une vigilance permanente. Les fraudeurs ne se contentent plus de dissimuler des marchandises derrière des parois aménagées ou au milieu de cargaisons ordinaires. Ils misent également sur la dispersion des colis, l’opacité sur leur propriété et la multiplicité des intermédiaires. Dans le cas présent, l’identification des propriétaires des colis constitue encore une zone d’ombre. Selon les éléments communiqués par les agents, le convoyeur aurait présenté le chargement comme constitué de marchandises diverses sans pouvoir préciser l’identité des propriétaires des produits prohibés. Le propriétaire du véhicule, A.A. Tall, de nationalité malienne, était présent pour s’expliquer. Il nie toutefois toute responsabilité dans le transport des marchandises saisies. L’absence du convoyeur et de l’apprenti au moment où les faux billets ont été découverts constitue également un élément que l’enquête devra éclaircir. Ces deux personnes pourraient, selon la Douane, détenir des informations déterminantes sur le chargement du véhicule, son itinéraire et l’identité des différents propriétaires des colis. Le Directeur général de la Douane burkinabè, Dr Yves Kafando, a indiqué : « Nous entendons ouvrir une procédure judiciaire ». Face à cette affaire aux ramifications encore à établir, le Directeur général des Douanes entend laisser la procédure judiciaire déterminer les responsabilités. Il a souligné que les faux billets et les produits prohibés seront conservés comme éléments matériels de la procédure avant leur transmission au procureur. Sous Dr Yves Kafando, la pression douanière ne faiblit pas Le premier responsable de l’administration douanière a également salué le professionnalisme des agents qui ont conduit le contrôle et la fouille du véhicule. À travers cette réaction, le Dr Yves Kafando réaffirme une ligne de conduite : ne laisser aucune zone grise sans investigation lorsqu’elle est susceptible de dissimuler une infraction économique ou financière. Depuis quelques années, il y a une constance dans la traque sans merci de la fraude au niveau de la Douane burkinabè. Cette nouvelle saisie intervient dans un contexte où les services douaniers sont appelés à jouer un rôle toujours plus déterminant dans la protection du tissu économique national. L'enjeu ne se limite plus à la perception des droits et taxes. Il concerne également la défense de la monnaie, la protection des consommateurs, la régulation des échanges et la lutte contre les circuits clandestins susceptibles d'alimenter la criminalité économique. Sous le leadership managérial du Dr Yves Kafando, la Douane burkinabè entend ainsi maintenir la pression sur les réseaux de fraude et de contrebande, en adaptant ses méthodes à l’évolution des techniques utilisées par les délinquants économiques. La saisie de Tenkodogo en est une illustration : 60 millions de francs CFA de faux billets n’entreront pas dans le circuit économique ; des produits prohibés ne parviendront pas à leurs destinataires ; et un véhicule servant au transport de cette cargaison a été immobilisé. Mais derrière les chiffres et les marchandises saisies se joue une bataille plus fondamentale : celle de la protection de l’économie nationale contre les flux financiers et commerciaux illicites. Dans cette confrontation, la Douane veut désormais faire passer un message clair aux réseaux de fraude : les modes opératoires peuvent changer, les itinéraires peuvent être déplacés, les marchandises peuvent être dissimulées, mais la vigilance douanière, elle, ne faiblit pas. Donatien FOFANA L’article Protection de l’économie nationale : La Douane burkinabè intensifie la traque des réseaux de fraude, 60 millions de faux billets stoppés est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .
